Perfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine plural. Form IV of '-m-n means to make safe, to grant security, to entrust. The community is defined by having performed this act of entering trust/security.

Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural. Root q-w-m carries standing, rising, establishing, maintaining. Here "qumtum ilā" means rising toward / intending / preparing for. The perfect tense with idhā gives it a future/habitual sense.

Conjunction fa (result/consequence) + imperative verb, Form I, 2mp. The fa- is jawāb ash-sharṭ (apodosis of the idhā condition). Root gh-s-l: to wash, to cleanse with water. This is the ONLY imperative of this root in the entire Quran.

Conjunction wa + imperative, Form I, 2mp. New action in the purification sequence. Root m-s-ḥ: to wipe, to pass the hand over, to anoint, to stroke. Critically, this is also the root of masīḥ (the anointed one / Christ). The shift from ghasala (wash) to masaḥa (wipe) marks a different mode of purification.
Perfect verb, 2mp, from kāna (to be). With in = conditional: "if you are/were." Root k-w-n: to be, to exist, to become. The most frequent verb root in the Quran (1396 occurrences).

Conjunction fa (consequential) + imperative, Form V (tafaʿʿala), 2mp. Form V of ṭ-h-r is reflexive-intensive: to purify oneself thoroughly. The tāʾ has assimilated into the ṭāʾ (idghām). This is the response-clause to the junub condition: full-body purification.
Perfect verb, 2mp, from kāna. Second occurrence in the ayah. Same grammatical function as word 19 but with different predicate (marḍā instead of junuban).

Perfect verb, Form I, 3ms. Root j-y-ʾ: to come, arrive, bring. Here introduces a third-person scenario within the second-person address: "or one of you came from..." The shift from 2mp to 3ms creates a euphemistic distancing.

Perfect verb, Form III (fāʿala), 2mp. Root l-m-s: to touch, to feel, to seek by touching. Form III (lāmasa) adds reciprocity/mutuality: to touch one another, to have mutual physical contact. The debate whether this means any touching or specifically sexual contact is one of the great fiqh disputes.

Imperfect verb (jussive after lam), 2mp. Root is properly و ج د (w-j-d), though the bundle tags it as j-d-d. Form I wajada: to find, to discover, to encounter. Here in the negative: "you did not find water."
Imperative, Form V (tafaʿʿala), 2mp; root y-m-m = to aim toward, to intend, to head for; tayammama = to direct oneself deliberately toward the earth for purification

Conjunction fa + imperative, Form I, 2mp. Second occurrence of m-s-ḥ imperative in the ayah (first was word 13 for wuḍūʾ wiping of heads). Here it is the wiping action for tayammum — wiping faces and hands with earth instead of water.

Imperfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3ms. Root r-w-d: to seek, to desire, to go gently. Form IV arāda = to intend, to will, to design, to purpose. First occurrence in the ayah (negated by mā). This is the key verb of the theological conclusion: what does the divine intend?
Imperfect verb, Form I, 3ms, subjunctive (manṣūb after lām); root j-ʿ-l = to make, to render, to place, to appoint

Imperfect verb, Form IV, 3ms. Second occurrence (first was word 48, negated). Now without negation: "but He DOES intend..." The subject (Allāh) is implied from context. The contrast: NOT constriction → BUT purification.
Imperfect verb, Form II (faʿʿala), 3ms, subjunctive + 2mp object pronoun -kum; Form II ṭahhara = to purify intensively (transitive) — God as agent of purification
Imperfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3ms, subjunctive (manṣūb after lām); root t-m-m = to be complete, whole, perfect

Imperfect verb, Form I, 2mp. Root sh-k-r: to be thankful, grateful; to recognize and acknowledge abundance; to flourish (of a plant). The ayah ends on gratitude — the entire purification system exists so that its recipients recognize divine generosity.
Imperative verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. Direct command to actively recall. Object is ni'mata llāhi (accusative). Transitive with explicit object.

Perfect verb, Form III (fā'ala), 3rd person masculine singular + 2mp object suffix -kum. Form III implies reciprocity: He entered mutual binding with you. This is the ONLY occurrence of this verb form in the entire Quran.
Perfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. Introduces quoted covenant-declaration.
Perfect verb, Form I, 1st person plural. Part of the quoted covenant-declaration. sam' encompasses both auditory reception and comprehension.
Perfect verb, Form IV (af'ala), 1st person plural. From ṭ-w-': to be willing, to submit. Form IV causative: to bring oneself into willing compliance. Completes the covenant formula with sami'nā.
Imperative verb, Form VIII (ifta'ala), 2nd person masculine plural. From w-q-y: to guard, protect. Form VIII reflexive: to guard oneself.

Form I perfect active, 3rd person masculine singular: wa'ada (he promised). Root w-'-d carries promising, threatening, and appointing. Takes a double object: direct object (alladhīna) and content clause (lahum maghfira...). The perfect tense presents the promise as already accomplished — fait accompli.

Form IV perfect active, 3rd person masculine plural: āmanū (they placed trust). Root '-m-n carries safety, security, trust, faithfulness. Form IV (afʿala) is causative: "they caused themselves to be secure" or "they entered into a state of trust/security." The perfect tense indicates a completed state — their trust is established.

Form I perfect active, 3rd person masculine plural: ʿamilū (they worked/labored). Root '-m-l carries doing, working, laboring, manufacturing. Unlike faʿala (general doing), ʿamila implies deliberate, effortful action. The perfect tense indicates completed labor — their deeds are established.

Form III imperfect active, 3rd person masculine plural. Form III (فَاعَلَ / fā'ala) indicates reciprocal or adversarial action: muḥāraba = to wage war against, to fight mutually. Transitive, taking Allah as direct object. This is the ONLY Form III imperfect occurrence in the Quran.

Form II passive subjunctive, 3rd person masculine plural. Form II (فَعَّلَ / fa''ala) indicates intensity, repetition, or plurality of action. The passive voice + subjunctive (after أَن) = "that they be killed." The Form II intensification distinguishes this from simple Form I قُتِلَ.

Form II passive subjunctive, 3rd person masculine plural. From ṣ-l-b: to be firm, hard; to crucify. Form II (فَعَّلَ) = intensive — crucifixion involves prolonged public display. Passive + subjunctive after أَوْ, continuing the penalty list.

Form II passive subjunctive, 3rd person feminine singular (feminine agreement with أَيْدِيهِمْ). From q-t-': to cut, sever, cut off. Form II = intensive/thorough cutting. This is the ONLY Form II passive (tuqaṭṭa'a) subjunctive in the Quran.

Form I passive subjunctive, 3rd person masculine plural. MASAQ assigns root ن ف س (n-f-s), but the actual verb is نَفَى (nafā) which can be analyzed from ن ف ي (n-f-y): to banish, exile, expel, negate. This is the ONLY passive occurrence of this verbal form in the Quran.

This is the ONLY Form IV occurrence in the Quran — a hapax of this specific conjugation.

Perfect verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala), 3rd person masculine plural. From w-q-y: to guard, protect, shield. Form VIII is reflexive: they guarded themselves. First of three occurrences (words 13, 22, 26). The constant through all three conditional stages.
Perfect verb, Form IV, 3rd person masculine plural. Second occurrence (cf. word 4). Here in Stage 1 of the conditional clause.
Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine plural. Second occurrence (cf. word 6). Here in Stage 1 condition.
Perfect verb, Form VIII, 3rd person masculine plural. Second occurrence (cf. word 13). Opens Stage 2.
Perfect verb, Form IV, 3rd person masculine plural. Third occurrence (cf. words 4, 15). Here in Stage 2. This is the final occurrence of āmanū — absent from Stage 3.
Perfect verb, Form VIII, 3rd person masculine plural. Third occurrence (cf. words 13, 20). Opens Stage 3 — the final and highest condition.
Perfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine plural. Causative: to cause ḥusn (beauty/goodness) to exist. Appears only in Stage 3, replacing both āmanū and ʿamilū ṣ-ṣāliḥāt.

Imperfect verb, Form IV (yufʿilu), 3rd person masculine singular. Active voice with Allāh as subject. The shift to imperfect tense (from the perfect tense conditions) signals ongoing, permanent love — not a one-time event.
Perfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine plural. Causative of amn: to produce security, to place trust. The formula yā ayyuhā lladhīna āmanū appears ~89 times in the Quran.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, with nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla (heavy emphasis nūn) + pronoun -kum (you, plural). MASAQ assigns root b-l-l but the standard lexical root for this verb is b-l-w (to test, try, wear out). The form is yablū with the heavy emphasis nūn making the action inescapable.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person feminine singular (subject: aydīkum), + pronoun -hu (referring to ṣayd or shayʾ). The verb tanālu is from n-y-l = to reach, attain, obtain. The clause describes the game as accessible.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive (manṣūb) governed by implicit ʾan after lām al-taʿlīl; subject is Allāh — the trial's purpose is divine ascertainment/exposure of the believers
Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular + pronoun -hu (Him, i.e. Allāh). From kh-w-f = to fear, be afraid, be in awe. Active present: the fearing is ongoing, habitual.
Perfect verb, Form VIII (iftiʿāla), 3rd person masculine singular. Form VIII of ʿ-d-w = to exceed bounds, transgress. The Form VIII intensifies reflexivity: he made himself a transgressor.

Perfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine plural. Causative of amn (security): to cause security to exist — to give trust, to believe. Transitivity: MIXED (300 with object, 58 without). Here used without explicit object — absolute trust.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural, jussive (majzūm by lā). From q-t-l: to kill, to slay. Transitivity: MIXED (57 with object, 2 without). Here transitive with aṣ-ṣayda as direct object. QIRAAT: tuqattilū [Irreg] — Form II intensive: "do not slaughter repeatedly."

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular + 3rd person masculine singular pronoun suffix (-hu referring to aṣ-ṣayd). Transitivity: TRANSITIVE (34/34 with object). The pronoun -hu refers back to aṣ-ṣayd (the game) — the killing that was just prohibited. QIRAAT: qattalahu [Irreg] — Form II intensive: "slaughtered it" (emphasizing brutality or repetition).

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Third occurrence of q-t-l in this ayah (after taqtulū and qatalahu). No pronoun suffix — the object is the preceding mā. The repetition of q-t-l three times in one ayah is striking: prohibition (taqtulū) → violation (qatalahu) → calibration (mā qatala). QIRAAT: qattala [Irreg] — Form II.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular (referring to the dual dhawā — singular verb with dual subject is standard). From ḥ-k-m: to judge, to restrain by wisdom, to exercise authority. Transitivity: MIXED (25 with object, 14 without). Here with bihi = "judges by it / concerning it."
notes: حكم is construed with بِهِ here

grammar: Compound purpose particle لِ (lām at-taʿlīl) + IV imperfect from dh-w-q (Form I), 3rd masculine singular, subjunctive (manṣūb by lām at-taʿlīl); transitive (19/19 with object); marks the telos of the entire penalty structure as direct experiential contact

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. From ʿ-f-w: to efface, to obliterate, to pardon. ʿAfā = He effaced/pardoned — with Allāh as subject. Transitivity: MIXED (9 with object, 1 without). Here with ʿammā (about/from what) — the pardon targets "what preceded."

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. From s-l-f: to precede, to go before, to be prior. Salafa = it preceded — referring to pre-legislation violations. Only 8 occurrences in the Quran. Transitivity: MIXED (5 with object, 2 without). Here without explicit object.

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. From ʿ-w-d: to return, to go back, to revert. ʿĀda = he returned — to the prohibited behavior. Transitivity: MIXED (3 with object, 1 without). Here without explicit object: absolute return to violation.

Imperfect verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. From n-q-m: to take vengeance, to exact retribution, to punish. Form VIII yantaqimu = He exacts retribution — reflexive intensive: He takes for Himself the act of punishment. Only 17 occurrences of this root in the Quran.

Perfect verb, passive voice (PV_PASS), Form I of ḥ-l-l. Passive subject is ṣaydu l-baḥr (the catch of the sea). The passive construction leaves the agent unspecified — the lawfulness is declared without naming who declares it (divine passive). Transitivity: TRANSITIVE (8 occurrences in PV_PASS, all with object).

Perfect verb, passive voice (PV_PASS), Form II (faʿʿala pattern → fuʿʿila passive). Passive subject is ṣaydu l-barr. Mirrors uḥilla structurally — same divine passive, opposite legal verdict. Form II intensification: not merely ḥaruma (became sacred) but ḥurrima (was made intensively sacred/forbidden).

Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural. From d-m-w: to last, continue, persist. Mā dumtum = as long as you persisted/remained. Transitivity: TRANSITIVE (4 with object, 0 without) per cache, though here used with predicate ḥuruman rather than a direct object (copulative construction).

Imperative verb (CV), 2nd person masculine plural. Form VIII (iftaʿala) of w-q-y: to guard, protect, shield. Ittaqū = guard yourselves, take God as your shield, be conscious of God. Transitivity: MIXED (90 with object, 2 without). Here transitive with Allāh as object.

Imperfect verb, passive voice (IV_PASS), 2nd person masculine plural. From ḥ-sh-r: to gather, assemble, drive together, herd. The passive indicates the gathering is done TO you — you do not choose to gather, you are driven. The imperfect tense suggests ongoing or future process.

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Takes double accusative: first object (al-kaʿba) and second object/resultant state (qiyāman). Transitivity: MIXED (238 with object, 1 without). Here clearly transitive with explicit objects.

Purposive PREP لِ (lām al-taʿlīl) + imperfect verb Form I, 2nd person masculine plural, subjunctive (manṣūb after lām); the lām introduces the teleological purpose clause — the entire Kaaba-month-offering-garland system exists for this epistemic purpose

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative (marfūʿ). Active knowing — divine knowledge in action. The imperfect aspect signals ongoing, continuous knowing — not a one-time event but perpetual awareness.

Imperative verb, Form I (faʿala), 2nd person masculine plural. From ʿ-l-m: to know, perceive, mark. The hamzat al-waṣl (ٱ) indicates the imperative. Governs two anna-clauses as its objects. Transitivity: here used with anna (that-clause) rather than direct object noun — without_object pattern per ROOT DATA.

Imperfect verb, Form I (faʿala → yafʿalu), 3rd person masculine singular. Active voice. From ʿ-l-m: to know, to be aware, to perceive. Imperfect tense indicates continuous, ongoing, habitual knowledge. MIXED transitivity (290 with object, 44 without). Here takes the relative clause mā tubdūna wa-mā taktumūna as its object.

Imperfect verb, Form IV (afʿala → yufʿilu), 2nd person masculine plural. Active voice. From b-d-d: to appear, to become manifest. Form IV = causative: to cause something to appear, to make visible, to disclose. TRANSITIVE (11 with object, 0 without). Here the object is elided — the relative pronoun mā captures whatever they reveal.

Imperfect verb, Form I (faʿala → yafʿulu), 2nd person masculine plural. Active voice. From k-t-m: to conceal, to suppress, to keep secret. TRANSITIVE (20 with object, 0 without). Here the object is elided — the relative pronoun mā captures whatever they conceal.
Imperative verb, 2nd person masculine singular. Command addressed to the Prophet. The form implies public proclamation.

Imperfect verb, Form VIII (istafʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. Form VIII of s-w-y: to seek equality/levelness with oneself — reflexive equalization. Subject is al-khabīthu (the foul), with wa-ṭ-ṭayyibu joined by wāw.

Perfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine singular + 2nd person masculine singular object suffix (-ka). The subject is kathratu l-khabīth (the abundance of the foul). Form IV is causative: to cause wonder/amazement IN someone.

Imperative verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala), 2nd person masculine plural. From w-q-y: to guard, shield, protect. Form VIII: to take a shield for oneself — reflexive self-protection. Object is Allāh (word 14).
Imperfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 2nd person masculine plural. From f-l-h: to split, to cleave (earth for planting), to succeed, to prosper. Form IV: to cause success/prosperity.

Perfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine plural. From '-m-n: to grant security, to make safe. Form IV: to bring oneself into a state of security/trust — to believe. Subject is the relative pronoun alladhīna.
Imperfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural, jussive mood (after lā nāhiya). From s-'-l: to ask, to question, to request. The jussive indicates command context.

Imperfect verb, Form IV passive (ufʿila), 3rd person feminine singular, jussive (after in). From b-d-d: to appear, to become manifest. Form IV passive: to be made to appear, to be disclosed. Subject is implicit (the things asked about).

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person feminine singular, jussive (apodosis of in-conditional). From s-w-': to be evil, to cause harm. Subject is implicit (the disclosed things). Object is the attached pronoun kum (you).

Imperfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural, jussive (after in). Same form as word 5, but now in a conditional protasis rather than a prohibition. The same act (asking) is reframed: prohibited in general, conditionally permitted during revelation.

Imperfect verb, Form II passive (yufaʿʿalu), 3rd person masculine singular. From n-z-l: to descend, to come down. Form II: to send down (repeatedly, intensively). The passive: is being sent down. Imperfect tense indicates ongoing process.

Same form as word 9. Form IV passive, jussive. Here functions as the apodosis of the second conditional (wa-in tasʾalū...tubda lakum). The repetition of tubda creates structural symmetry between the two conditionals.

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. From '-f-w: to efface, to obliterate traces, to pardon. Subject is Allāh (following word). The perfect tense indicates a completed action — pardon already enacted.
perfect verb (PV), form I, 3rd person masculine singular (collective agreement with qawm), transitive with attached feminine singular object pronoun -hā
perfect verb (PV), form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine plural, kāna-type copula (incomplete verb taking predicate kāfirīna)
perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular; ja'ala here means "to institute, to designate, to render" — with mā, negates that God ever established these categories
perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine plural; kafara = to cover, to conceal, to deny, to be ungrateful; perfect tense marks the kufr as an established completed state

imperfect verb (IV tag in MASAQ = Form VIII iftarā/yaftarī), 3rd person masculine plural; Form VIII of f-t-r — reflexive fabrication, to invent something from oneself; imperfect tense = ongoing, habitual fabrication

imperfect verb (IV tag in MASAQ = Form I 'aqala/ya'qilu), 3rd person masculine plural; '-q-l = to hobble (a camel), to bind, to restrain, to use reason; imperfect = ongoing capacity; negated by lā = they do not reason
Perfect passive verb (PV_PASS), 3rd person masculine singular. Passive voice: the speaker is deliberately unspecified, making the call universal. From root q-w-l (to say, speak, declare).

Perfect active verb (PV), Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. Subject: Allāh. Form IV of n-z-l: causative descent — He caused to come down. Implies deliberate, authoritative transmission from above to below.
Perfect active verb (PV), 3rd person masculine plural. Active voice — contrasting with the passive qīla. They actively choose to speak their refusal. Subject is the implied they (those addressed).
Perfect active verb (PV), 1st person plural. From root w-j-d: to find, discover, come upon. Transitive: they found their forefathers upon something. 39 Quranic occurrences as PV.

Perfect verb (PV), 3rd person masculine singular. Copular verb: introduces the predicate state of their forefathers. Combined with awa-law creates the hypothetical frame: even if their forefathers WERE such that...

Imperfect active verb (IV), 3rd person masculine plural. From root ʿ-l-m: to know, to have knowledge. Here negated by lā — they do not know. Used WITHOUT explicit object (intransitive reading: they possess no knowledge at all).

Imperfect active verb (IV), 3rd person masculine plural. Form VIII (iftaʿala) of h-d-y: to be guided, find guidance. Reflexive: to seek/find one's own way. Combined with lā: they were not able to find guidance on their own. 109 Quranic occurrences in Form IV (imperfect).

Perfect verb, Form IV (afʿala), 3rd person masculine plural. Form IV of '-m-n: to cause safety/to enter into a state of security-through-trust. Transitivity: MIXED — 300 with object (believe in X), 58 without (believe/commit absolutely).

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular + 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun -kum. Transitivity: TRANSITIVE (23 occurrences, all with object). The doubled rāʾ (ḍ-r-r) is a geminate root.

Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Transitivity: MIXED (44 with object, 10 without). Here used without explicit object — absolute intransitive: they strayed (from the path, implied).

Perfect verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala), 2nd person masculine plural. Form VIII of h-d-y: to seek and find guidance for oneself — reflexive-effortful. Transitivity: MIXED (49 with object, 6 without). Here used without object — absolute: you guided yourselves.

Imperfect verb, Form II (faʿʿala), 3rd person masculine singular + 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun -kum. Form II of n-b-ʾ: to inform with weight, to deliver significant news. Transitivity: MIXED (34 with object, 1 without). The implicit subject is Allāh.
Perfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. Auxiliary/copular verb establishing habitual past: kuntum + imperfect taʿmalūna = "you used to do" / "you were doing" — continuous past action.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. Transitivity: MIXED (138 with object, 28 without). Here used without explicit object — the doing/working is absolute, covering all domains of action.
Perfect verb, Form IV, 3rd person masculine plural. Causative: to cause security (amn) to exist — to trust, believe.
Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is al-mawt (death). Object is aḥadakum (one of you). Transitive.
Perfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. Here: ḍaraba fī l-arḍ = to travel, journey (lit: to strike into the land).
Perfect verb, Form IV, 3rd person feminine singular (agreeing with muṣība). From s-w-b: to hit the mark, to befall.
Imperfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural + dual pronoun -humā. Only 2 Quranic occurrences of this root.
Imperfect verb, Form IV, 3rd person masculine dual. From q-s-m: to divide; Form IV: to swear (to divide by oath).
Perfect verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala), 2nd person masculine plural. Reflexive/intensive of doubt.
Imperfect verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala), 1st person plural. From sh-r-y: to buy/sell (semantically bidirectional).
Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Copulative: "even if it were..."
Imperfect verb, Form I, 1st person plural. From k-t-m: to conceal, suppress, hide.
perfect verb, passive voice (PV_PASS), 3ms
perfect verb, active (PV), X-form, 3rd masculine dual
imperfect verb, active (IV form reading or Form I), 3md
perfect verb, active (PV), X-form, 3ms
imperfect verb, active (IV), 3md
perfect verb, active (PV), VIII-form, 1pp

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine plural, subjunctive (manṣūb by an). From ʾ-t-y. Here used with bi- (instrumental/accompaniment preposition): yaʾtū bi- = to bring, to come with, to produce.
Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine plural, subjunctive (manṣūb by an — parallel to yaʾtū). From kh-w-f.
Imperfect verb, Form I passive (yuraddu → turadda, feminine for aymān), subjunctive (manṣūb by an). From r-d-d. Passive voice: the oaths are returned, not they return them.
Imperative verb, Form VIII, 2nd person masculine plural. From w-q-y (to protect, to guard). Form VIII (ittaqā): reflexive protection — to shield oneself, to be on guard, to be conscious.
Imperative verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. From s-m-ʿ. Absolute/intransitive use — no explicit object. This is the without-object pattern (cf. 7:204, 50:41).
Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. From h-d-y. Negated by lā. Subject: Allāh. Object: al-qawma l-fāsiqīna.

Imperfect verb, form I, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative (marfūʿ). Active voice — Allāh is the agent. Takes a direct object (ar-rusula). The imperfect tense for a future event creates narrative vividness (ḥikāya).

Imperfect verb, form I, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative (marfūʿ). The subject is Allāh (from the previous clause). Imperfect for a future event — vivid present. Takes the following question (mādhā ujibtum) as its direct speech content (maqūl al-qawl).

Perfect verb, form IV (ufʿila pattern), passive voice, 2nd person masculine plural. From j-w-b: the passive ujībtu means "I was answered/responded to." The messengers are the recipients of responses — what came back to them from their communities.

Perfect verb, form I, 3rd person masculine plural. The subject is the messengers (ar-rusul). Shifts to past tense despite the future scene — the response is narrated as already completed (ḥikāya), creating certainty about the outcome.
perfect verb Form I, 3ms
imperative verb Form I, 2ms
perfect verb Form II, 1s + 2ms object pronoun
imperfect verb Form II, 2ms
perfect verb Form II, 1s + 2ms object pronoun
imperfect verb Form I, 2ms

grammar: imperfect verb Form I, 2ms
imperfect verb Form I, 3fs (or 2ms)
imperfect verb Form IV, 2ms
imperfect verb Form IV, 2ms
perfect verb Form I, 1s
perfect verb Form I, 2ms + 3mp object pronoun
perfect verb Form I, 3ms

Perfect verb, Form IV (ʾafʿala), first person singular. The subject is God (divine first person). awḥā = to inspire, to reveal, to communicate rapidly and subtly. The verb is used here without an explicit direct object — the content of the waḥy is introduced by the masdariyya ʾan. Transitivity: MIXED — this is one of 5 without-object occurrences of w-h-y PV (5:111, 19:11, 26:52, 35:31, 99:5).

Imperative verb (command form), Form IV (ʾafʿala), second person masculine plural. From ʾ-m-n: to be secure, to trust, to believe. āminū is the command form: "believe!" or "place your trust!" This is the content of God's waḥy to the disciples — they are commanded to believe. Transitivity: MIXED — this is one of 6 without-object occurrences of ʾ-m-n CV (2:13, 2:91, 3:72, 4:136, 5:111, 64:8).

Perfect verb, Form I, third person masculine plural. From q-w-l: to say, to speak, to declare. Introduces the disciples' response in direct speech. The shift from divine imperative (āminū) to human declarative (qālū) marks the transition from command to compliance.

Perfect verb, Form IV, first person plural. From ʾ-m-n: to be secure, to trust. āmannā = "we have believed/placed our trust." This is the disciples' direct response to the command āminū — morphologically perfect (completed action), indicating their belief is not pending but accomplished. Transitivity: without object — one of 58 objectless ʾ-m-n PV occurrences.

Imperative verb, Form I, second person masculine singular. From sh-h-d: to witness, to testify, to be present, to observe. ishhad = "bear witness!" or "attest!" The addressee is ambiguous — it can be directed at Jesus or at God. The singular imperative within a dialogue supposedly between the disciples and God (via waḥy) creates a structural tension about who is being asked to witness.
notes: content_via_bi

grammar: Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is al-ḥawāriyyūna (the disciples — masculine plural). The singular verb preceding a plural subject is standard Arabic syntax.

Imperfect verb, Form X (istafʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. Subject: rabbuka (your Lord). Form X of ṭ-w-ʿ: to seek obedience/compliance, hence to be able/capable — capacity as seeking the thing's compliance with one's will.

Imperfect verb, Form II (faʿʿala), 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb after an). Form II of n-z-l: intensive/causative sending-down — gradual or repeated descent. Object: māʾidatan.
Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject: ʿĪsā (implied). The second qāla in this ayah, now introducing ʿĪsā's response.

Command verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala), 2nd person masculine plural. Object: Allāha. From w-q-y: to protect, to guard, to shield. Form VIII: reflexive protection — shield yourselves through consciousness of God.

Perfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. Used with in to create past-conditional: if you have been (in a state of faith). The perfect tense probes existing/established faith, not future intention.

Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural. From q-w-l: to say, to speak, to declare. Introduces the disciples' (al-ḥawāriyyīn) speech in response to ʿĪsā's question in 5:112. The plural subject pronoun refers to the disciples collectively.

Imperfect verb, 1st person plural, Form IV (ʾarāda/yurīdu). From r-w-d: to go about, to seek, to desire, to want. Form IV (ʾarāda) = to want, to intend, to will. The shift from perfect (qālū) to imperfect (nurīdu) within the same speech marks ongoing, present-tense desire — they continue to want.
Imperfect verb, 1st person plural, Form I, subjunctive mood (manṣūb by an). From '-k-l: to eat, to consume, to devour, to corrode. The first of four subjunctive verbs governed by an.
notes: partitive_min_fills_context

grammar: Imperfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb, coordinated with na'kula through wāw). Quadriliteral root ṭ-m-'-n. The verb agrees with the feminine plural qulūb (hearts) using feminine singular agreement (standard for non-rational plurals/broken plurals).
Imperfect verb, 1st person plural, Form I, subjunctive mood (manṣūb, coordinated through wāw). From '-l-m: to know, to be aware, to mark, to learn. The third of four subjunctive verbs.

Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, with 1st person plural object pronoun -nā. From ṣ-d-q: to be truthful, to speak truth, to fulfill a promise, to be sincere. The 2nd person addresses ʿĪsā directly — "you have been truthful to us."

Imperfect verb, 1st person plural, Form I copula, subjunctive mood (manṣūb, coordinated through wāw). From k-w-n: to be, to exist, to become, to come into being. Functions as a copular verb linking the subject (we) to the predicate (mina sh-shāhidīna).
Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Introduces direct speech. Subject is ʿĪsā (word 2).
Imperative verb, Form IV (afʿala), 2nd person masculine singular. Form IV is causative: to cause to descend. Addressed to Allāh. Object: māʾida. Only 2 occurrences of this exact CV form in the Quran.
Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person feminine singular. Subject is māʾida (the table). Copulative function: the table BECOMES/IS a celebration and sign. Indicative mood (marfūʿ).
Imperative verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine singular, with 1st person plural object pronoun -nā. From r-z-q: to provide sustenance, to grant livelihood. Addressed to Allāh.
Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular. Introduces direct divine speech. The subject is Allāh (following word). Transitive — governs the entire quoted clause as its object.

Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), 3rd person masculine singular, jussive mood (majzūm by man al-sharṭiyya). Form I kafara/yakfuru. Here used without explicit direct object. MIXED transitivity (59 with object, 8 without): without_object ayahs include 2:91, 2:256, 3:70, 3:98, 3:101, 4:136, 14:8, 19:82. The absence of object here leaves the scope of kufr unspecified — covers what? Disbelieves in what?

Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), 1st person singular, indicative (marfūʿ). Form II ʿadhdha-ba/yuʿadhdhibu. The -hū pronoun suffix is the direct object (whoever disbelieves). Form II = intensive/causative of the root. First of three occurrences of root ʿ-dh-b in this ayah.

Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), 1st person singular, indicative. Form II. Third occurrence of root ʿ-dh-b. The -hū pronoun here is ambiguous: it could refer back to ʿadhāban (I have not punished with it) or be a resumptive pronoun for the relative clause. Functions inside the relative clause modifying ʿadhāban.
notes: clitic_resumes_punishment

grammar: Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is Allāh. From q-w-l: to say, to speak, to utter. The perfect tense here narrates a future event (Day of Judgment) as accomplished fact, a Quranic technique for certainty.
Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular. From q-w-l: to say. Direct address to Jesus — "did you say?" The perfect tense refers to a completed past action: the alleged utterance.

Form VIII imperative or indicative, 2nd person masculine plural + 1st person object suffix. From '-kh-dh: to take, to seize. Form VIII ittakhadha = to take for oneself, to adopt, to appropriate. The Form VIII adds a reflexive/self-directed dimension: not just taking, but deliberately adopting for oneself.
Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is ʿĪsā (Jesus). Introduces Jesus's response to the divine interrogation. Second occurrence of qāla in the ayah — now the respondent speaks.

Imperfect verb (fiʿl muḍāriʿ), 3rd person masculine singular. From k-w-n: to be, to exist, to become. Here used as a copula: "it is [not] for me" = "it is [not] fitting/possible for me." The imperfect indicates ongoing impossibility, not a past event.
Imperfect verb, 1st person singular, subjunctive (manṣūb by ʾan). From q-w-l: to say. Jesus's own speech act is what is being denied: "that I should say."
Perfect verb, 1st person singular. From k-w-n: to be. Here as auxiliary in a compound tense: kuntu qultuhū = "I had said it" — pluperfect construction expressing a past hypothetical.
Perfect verb, 1st person singular, with 3rd masculine singular object suffix (-hū). "I had said it" — the hypothetical utterance. The object suffix -hū refers to the alleged claim of dual divinity.
Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, with 3rd masculine singular object suffix (-hū). From '-l-m: to know, to be aware, to have knowledge. Here addressing God: "You would have known it."

Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular. From '-l-m: to know. Addresses God directly: "You know what is in my self." The shift from perfect (ʿalimtahū) to imperfect (taʿlamu) marks a move from hypothetical past knowledge to ongoing present knowledge.

Imperfect verb, 1st person singular. From '-l-m: to know. "I do not know" — Jesus's admission of the limits of creaturely knowledge. The third occurrence of '-l-m in the defense section, now in the 1st person negative.
Perfect verb, Form I, 1st person singular. From q-w-l (to say). MASAQ assigns q-l-l but the functional root is q-w-l. Perfect tense in a defense context: completed speech-act being reported.
Perfect verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine singular with 1st person object suffix. Root '-m-r: to command, to order. MIXED transitivity (18 with object, 2 without).
Imperative verb (CV), 2nd person masculine plural. Root '-b-d: worship, serve. MIXED transitivity (35 with object, 2 without). The commanded content.
Perfect verb, 1st person singular. Copular kāna: past state. With shahīdan as predicate: I was a witness. Time-bounded by mā dumtu fīhim.
Perfect verb, 1st person singular. Root d-m-w: to persist, endure, last. TRANSITIVE (4/0). Only 4 PV occurrences in Quran.

Perfect verb, Form V, 2nd person masculine singular with 1st person object suffix. Root w-f-y: to be full, complete. MIXED transitivity (7/1). THE pivotal word — its meaning determines death, ascension, or full reckoning.
Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular. Copular kāna addressed to God. Parallel to kuntu (word 15) but shifted from 1st to 2nd person — authority transfers.

Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, active, indicative (marfūʿ). Root ʿ-l-n. Form IV (ʾafʿala): causative — "to make something open/public." 10 IV occurrences. The antithetical counterpart of yusirrūna (word 7). Together they form an exhaustive merism: hidden + open = everything. TRANS transitivity. Uncommon root (16 total occurrences).

Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, active, indicative (marfūʿ). Root ḥ-b-b. Form IV (ʾafʿala): "to love, to like." 63 IV occurrences — common form. The subject is the implied "He" (God, from innahu). MIXED transitivity (62 with obj, 1 without). The direct object is al-mustakbirīna. The formula lā yuḥibbu + [category] appears repeatedly in Quran (3:32, 3:57, 4:36, 16:23, 28:76, 42:27, 57:23) as a categorical divine judgment.

Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3ms. Root sh-y-ʾ. The first of three occurrences of this root in the ayah. Here in perfect tense within the contrafactual — "had He willed" = but He did not so will. Subject: Allāh (word 4).

Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3ms. Root j-ʿ-l. Transitive with double object: jaʿala-kum (you = first object) ummatan (community = second object/complement). In the apodosis of law-conditional = unrealized action.

Imperfect verb (IV), Form IV, 3ms. Root ḍ-l-l. Form IV (ʾafʿala) = causative: "causes to stray" (vs Form I ḍalla = "strayed"). Imperfect tense = ongoing, habitual action — this is what God continually does, not a one-time act.

Imperfect verb (IV), Form I, 3ms. Root sh-y-ʾ. Second occurrence in the ayah. Here in imperfect tense (vs perfect shāʾa in word 3) — ongoing willing in the real world, not hypothetical. The subject is grammatically ambiguous: it could be Allāh ("whom HE wills") or the referent of man ("whoever [himself] wills").
Imperfect verb (IV), Form I, 3ms. Root h-d-y. Antonym of yuḍillu (word 11). Imperfect tense matches yuḍillu — parallel structure. Subject is Allāh (implicit, carried from previous clause).

Imperfect verb (IV), Form I, 3ms. Root sh-y-ʾ. Third occurrence of the root in this ayah. Exact repetition of word 13. The triple occurrence (shāʾa, yashāʾu, yashāʾu) forms the rhythmic and theological backbone of the ayah.

Imperfect verb (IV), Form I, 2mp passive (internal passive: tusʾalūna → tusʾalunna with nūn al-tawkīd thaqīla). Root s-ʾ-l. The passive voice removes the questioner's identity — focus is on the subjects being questioned, not who questions them. Nūn al-tawkīd thaqīla (heavy nūn) adds maximum emphasis.

Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 2mp. Root k-w-n. In combination with the following imperfect (taʿmalūna), forms the kāna + imperfect periphrastic construction = habitual past action: "you used to do / you were doing."

Imperfect verb (IV), Form I, 2mp active. Root ʿ-m-l. Final word of the ayah. The imperfect in kāna + taʿmalūna = habitual past. No explicit object — the verb is used absolutely: "what you were doing" (the mā in ʿammā provides the general object).

Form I imperative (CV), 2ms. Apocopated (majzūm) — the lām is quiescent. Commands the Prophet to speak what follows. The most frequent imperative in the Quran.

Form II perfect verb (PV), 3ms + attached pronoun -hu (3ms accusative = "it," referring to the Quran). Form II (faʿʿala) adds iterative/intensive meaning to Form I nazala (to descend): "to send down repeatedly / in stages."

Form II imperfect verb (IV tag in bundle = verb), 3ms, subjunctive (manṣūb by lām al-taʿlīl). Form II (faʿʿala) is causative: "to cause to be firm." Subject is rūḥ al-qudus or God (implicit). COUNT=19 — uncommon root.

Form IV perfect verb (PV), 3mp. Form IV (afʿala) is causative of the base meaning "to be safe/secure" — so āmana literally = "to make oneself safe" or "to place trust in." COUNT=878 — one of the most frequent roots.

Form IV imperfect verb (yufʿilūna), 3rd person masculine plural. Root '-m-n. Form IV causative: "to cause (someone/something) to be secure" → "to believe, to place trust in." With bi- preposition: "to believe in, to place trust in." The imperfect indicates ongoing, habitual action. TRANSITIVITY: IV:MIXED(137obj/43no_obj) — here with explicit bi-prepositional object.

Form I imperfect verb (yafʿilu), 3rd person masculine singular, with attached pronoun -him (3mp, referring to alladhīna). Root h-d-y. The verb takes a direct object pronoun: "He guides THEM." TRANSITIVITY: IV:MIXED(102obj/7no_obj) — predominantly transitive. The ḍamma on the mīm of -him is epenthetic for liaison with the following word.

Form VIII imperfect verb (yaftaʿilu), 3ms. From f-r-y: to cut, to fashion, to fabricate. The Form VIII (iftirāʾ) adds reflexive/self-involvement — the fabricator invests himself in the construction of the lie. Imperfect tense: ongoing, habitual action, not a one-time event. Subject is delayed (alladhīna). Direct object: al-kadhib.

Form IV imperfect verb (yuʾminūna), 3mp. From ʾ-m-n: to be safe, secure. Form IV (āmana) = to grant safety, to place trust, to believe. The imperfect with lā indicates habitual non-belief. TRANSITIVITY: IV:MIXED(137obj/43no_obj) — here used with bi- (prepositional object), not a direct accusative.

Perfect verb (faʿala), 3ms, Form I. Root k-f-r. Primary sense: to cover, conceal. The perfect tense treats the disbelief as a completed act. Intransitive here (no direct object); the preposition bi- introduces the object of disbelief.

Perfect verb, passive voice (PV_PASS), 3ms, Form IV. Root k-r-h: to dislike, to hate, to be averse. Form IV (ʾakraha) = to compel, to coerce — causative of disliking. Passive: "was compelled/coerced." The agent of compulsion is suppressed — who coerced is left unstated.

Perfect verb (faʿala), 3ms, Form I. Root sh-r-ḥ: to open, to expand, to lay bare, to cut open (as in dissection), to explain. Here: "opened/expanded [his chest] to disbelief." The verb takes ṣadran as tamyīz (accusative of specification). Rare root: COUNT=5 in Quran.
notes: صَدْرًا is annotated as accusative specification

grammar: Form X perfect verb (istafʿala), 3mp. Root ḥ-b-b. Form X here carries the meaning of seeking/choosing/preferring — istaḥabba = to prefer one thing over another, to find lovable, to choose with deliberation. Takes a direct object (al-ḥayāt) and a comparative preposition (ʿalā). The wāw of the plural suffix carries a small alif (ṣilat al-wāw).
Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), Form I, 3ms. Root h-d-y. Subject is Allāh. Takes a direct object (al-qawm). lā yahdī = "does not guide." The imperfect tense with lā indicates a general, ongoing principle.
perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, active voice

grammar: Form III perfect verb (fāʿala), 3mp. The Form III pattern indicates reciprocal or intensive action — not merely "leaving" but a mutual severing or deliberate, purposeful departure. No explicit object — verb used intransitively here.

Perfect verb passive (PV_PASS), 3mp. Root f-t-n. Passive voice — they are the recipients of the trial, not the agents. The passive leaves the agent of testing unspecified (though contextually God or persecutors).
Form III perfect verb (fāʿala), 3mp. Root j-h-d. Form III indicates direction of effort toward someone/something — reciprocal or intensive exertion. No explicit object — used intransitively.
Form I perfect verb (faʿala), 3mp. Root ṣ-b-r. Used intransitively here. Completes the three-verb sequence: hājarū → jāhadū → ṣabarū.

Form I imperfect verb (IV tag in MASAQ = imperfect verb), 3fs. Subject: kullu nafsin (every soul, grammatically feminine because nafs is feminine). The imperfect within a yawma clause functions as a narrative present describing a future scene with vivid immediacy.

Form III imperfect verb, 3fs. Form III (mufāʿala) indicates reciprocal or intensive action: not merely speaking but engaging in back-and-forth argumentation. Functions as ḥāl (circumstantial clause) describing the state of the soul when it arrives — "comes while disputing." No explicit object — the verb is used intransitively here with ʿan marking the beneficiary.

Form II passive imperfect verb, 3fs. tuwaffā < waffā (Form II) = to pay in full, to complete. The passive voice (tufaʿʿalu) removes the agent — the one who repays is unnamed (divine passive). Subject: kullu nafsin. The verb governs mā ʿamilat as its second object (the content of what is repaid).

Form I perfect verb, 3fs + tāʾ al-taʾnīth (feminine marker agreeing with nafs). Root ʿ-m-l = to do, to work, to produce. The perfect tense marks completed action — the deeds are already done before the Day arrives. Very common root (360 occurrences). TRANSITIVITY: PV is MIXED (94obj/5no_obj) — here used with mā as the fronted object.

Form I passive imperfect verb, 3mp. Pattern yufʿalūna (passive of yafʿilūna). Root ẓ-l-m = to wrong, to oppress; also: to place in darkness. The passive voice + negation = "they are not wronged" — a divine guarantee. IV_PASS has 21 occurrences, showing this passive construction is a frequent Quranic formula.

Perfect verb (PV), 3ms. Root ḍ-r-b. Here in the idiom ḍaraba mathalan = "set forth a parable." The subject is Allāh (word 3). Transitive: takes mathalan as direct object and qaryatan as a second accusative (badal or ʿaṭf bayān).

Perfect verb (PV), 3fs. Root k-w-n. Copular function: introduces the prior state of the town. The tāʾ al-taʾnīth agrees with qaryatan (feminine). Takes two active-participle predicates: āminatan and muṭmaʾinnatan.

Imperfect verb (IV), 3ms. Root ʾ-t-y. The subject is rizquhā (word 10). The pronoun -hā refers back to qaryatan. The imperfect tense indicates ongoing, habitual action — provision was continuously arriving.
Perfect verb (PV), 3fs. Root k-f-r. The feminine singular agrees with qaryatan — the town as an entity denied. Takes the preposition bi- to mark what was denied (anʿum Allāh).

Perfect verb (PV), 3ms, Form IV (afʿala). Root dh-w-q. Causative of dhāqa (to taste): "He made [her/it] taste." The pronoun -hā refers to the town. God is the subject. Takes libāsa as a second object (double-accusative construction: made-it-taste [the garment]).

Perfect verb (PV), 3mp. Root k-w-n. The masculine plural shifts from the feminine singular of the town (kafarat) to its male inhabitants. With imperfect yaṣnaʿūna, forms the kāna + imperfect construction indicating habitual past action.

Imperfect verb (IV), 3mp. Root ṣ-n-ʿ. Indicates deliberate, skilled production — not casual action. The imperfect within kāna-frame = habitual past. No explicit object: the verb is used absolutely, leaving what they were crafting unspecified.

Perfect verb (PV), 3rd person masculine singular. Root j-y-ʾ. The attached pronoun -hum (them) makes this transitive: "he came TO them." The verb takes rasūlun as its subject (delayed fāʿil). COUNT: 276, all PV — the root appears ONLY as a perfect verb in the Quran, never imperfect, never imperative.

Form II perfect verb (faʿʿala), 3rd person masculine plural + attached pronoun -hu (him). Form II of k-dh-b is CAUSATIVE/DECLARATIVE: not merely "they lied" but "they declared him a liar / they called his message false." TRANSITIVITY: PV MIXED (92obj/30no_obj). Here transitive with -hu.

Perfect verb (PV), 3rd person masculine singular. Root ʾ-kh-dh. Here the subject is al-ʿadhāb (the punishment), making the punishment the active agent of seizure. TRANSITIVITY: PV MIXED (140obj/2no_obj) — overwhelmingly transitive. COUNT: 273. The verb is forceful: akhadha implies sudden, overwhelming capture.

grammar: Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative mood (marfū'). Subject is al-Qur'ān. Takes an indirect object via li- (lillatī). The imperfect tense indicates continuous, ongoing guidance — not a completed act.

Form II imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative mood. Subject is al-Qur'ān (from the inna-clause). Form II (fa''ala) is intensive/causative of Form I — intensified delivery of news. Takes direct object (al-mu'minīna) and content clause (anna lahum ajran kabīran).

Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, indicative mood. Subject is the implicit "they" referring back to al-mu'minīna via alladhīna. Takes direct object aṣ-ṣāliḥāt. The imperfect indicates habitual, ongoing action.

Form IV imperfect, 3rd person masculine plural, active voice. From root '-m-n (security, safety, trust). Form IV (afʿala) = causative: "to make safe, to make trustworthy, to grant security to." With bi- preposition: "to place trust in, to believe in, to consider secure/reliable." Transitivity: MIXED (137 with object, 43 without). Here used with bi-l-ākhirati as prepositional object.

Form VIII perfect, 1st person plural, active voice. From root '-d-d (to count, to number, to prepare). Form VIII (iftaʿala) = reflexive/intensive: "to prepare for oneself, to make ready with intent." The perfect tense signals completed action — the preparation is already done. Subject is the divine "We" (naḥnu). Direct object: ʿadhāban (punishment). Transitivity: TRANSITIVE (34/34 with object in ROOT DATA).

Form I imperfect (muḍāriʿ) verb, 3rd person masculine singular, active voice. Subject: al-insān. The final wāw is graphically dropped (apocopated spelling) though phonetically present (yadʿū). Takes bi-l-sharri as prepositional complement. Intransitive use with bi- marking the content of invocation.

Perfect tense verb (fiʿl māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular. Subject: al-insān. Takes ʿajūlā as predicate (khabar kāna, accusative). kāna here expresses a permanent state, not past tense — "the human IS [by nature] hasty."

Perfect verb, Form IV (arāda), first person plural "We" (majestic plural). Direct object is the following subjunctive clause (an nuhlika). The nā suffix marks divine agency. Transitivity: fully transitive (46/46 PV occurrences take objects per bundle).

Imperfect subjunctive, Form IV (ahlaka), first person plural. Subjunctive due to preceding أَنْ. Form IV is causative: "to cause to perish, to destroy." Transitivity: fully transitive (13/13 IV occurrences take objects). The object is qaryatan.

Perfect verb, Form I (amara), first person plural. Takes mutrafīhā as direct object. Transitivity: MIXED (18/20 with object, 2/20 without). Here transitive with a direct object. Key debate: what was commanded? The object of the command is elided — the affluent are commanded but the content of the command is unspecified.

Perfect verb, Form I (fasaqa), third person masculine plural. No explicit direct object — here used intransitively (cf. transitivity: MIXED, 3/4 with object, 1/4 without; 10:33 without object). The plural -ū refers to the mutrafīn.

Perfect verb, Form I (ḥaqqa), third person masculine singular. Subject is al-qawlu (the word/decree). Transitivity: MIXED (7/11 with object, 4/11 without). Here used with ʿalā (against it) indicating the decree falling upon/against the settlement.

Perfect verb, Form II (dammara), first person plural + object suffix -hā (referring to qaryatan). Form II is intensive/causative: "to demolish thoroughly, to shatter completely." Transitivity: MIXED (6/7 with object, 1/7 without at 47:10).
perfect verb (PV), Form IV (af'ala), first person plural, active — causative of halaka (to perish)

Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. Functions here as auxiliary establishing a habitual or ongoing state rather than simple past. Subject is the implied referent of man.
Imperfect indicative (marfūʿ), 3rd person masculine singular, Form IV (ʾafʿala). Subject is the referent of man. Takes al-ʿājilata as direct object.

Perfect verb, Form II (faʿʿala), 1st person plural. Form II intensifies the root meaning — not mere haste but active acceleration. Subject is divine "We." Takes an implied double object (lahū + mā nashāʾu).
Imperfect indicative (marfūʿ), 1st person plural, Form I. Subject is divine "We." Used here absolutely (intransitive) — "We will" without specifying the object (which is supplied by mā).
Imperfect indicative (marfūʿ), 1st person plural, Form IV (ʾafʿala). Subject is divine "We." Used here absolutely — the object is implied (the person referenced by man).
Perfect verb, Form I (faʿala), 1st person plural. Takes a double object: lahū (for him) + jahannama (Jahannam). Means "We assigned/rendered/made" — creative-designative action.

Imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I. Takes the feminine pronoun hā (referring to Jahannam) as direct object suffix. The verb is in ḥāl (circumstantial) position, describing the state of the subject after jaʿalnā.

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), Form IV (afʿala), third person masculine singular. From r-w-d: to go about seeking, to desire, to intend. Form IV intensifies: to bring about desire, to will deliberately. Object: al-ākhirata. Transitive (46 PV occurrences all transitive per bundle).

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), Form I, third person masculine singular. From s-'-y: to walk, to hasten, to strive, to exert oneself. Intransitive here (lahā provides the directional object via preposition). 5 PV occurrences total; MIXED transitivity (4 with object, 1 without in 53:39).

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), Form I, third person masculine singular. From k-w-n: to be, to exist, to become. Subject: saʿyuhum (their striving). kāna here does NOT indicate past tense but rather expresses a permanent, timeless truth (kāna al-istimrāriyya).

First person plural imperfect indicative (muḍāriʿ marfūʿ). Form I of m-d-d with shadda on dāl (geminate root). Subject is divine "We" (majestic plural). The imperfect indicates ongoing, continuous action — provision is not a one-time event.

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), third person masculine singular. Copular verb linking ʿaṭāʾu rabbika (subject) to maḥẓūran (predicate). Negated by mā — "the gift of your sustainer was never..." The perfect tense with mā creates a permanent negation spanning all time.

Form I imperative, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive-apocopated (unẓur). Addresses the Prophet or any addressee. Object is the interrogative clause kayfa faḍḍalnā. MIXED transitivity: 36 with object, 11 without in CV form.

Form II perfect, 1st person plural (divine "We"). Intensifies Form I faḍala (to surpass, be left over). Transitive with direct object baʿḍahum. Transitivity flag: TRANSITIVE (17/17 with object). The -nā suffix is the majestic plural (pluralis majestatis).

Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive mood (مجزوم, majzūm) — apocopated by preceding lā al-nāhiya. Form I. Takes double accusative: first object = ilāhan, second object/complement = implied status alongside God.

Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (منصوب, manṣūb) — governed by the preceding fā' al-sababiyya after lā al-nāhiya. Form I. Used metaphorically: "to end up in a state" rather than literal sitting.

grammar: Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), 3rd person masculine plural. Functions as a copular verb (fi'l nāqiṣ) — linking subject (al-mubadhdhirīn, governed by inna) to predicate (ikhwān). The Quranic "kāna of characterization" — establishes a timeless trait, not a mere past event.
Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular. Copular (nāqiṣ) verb linking ash-shayṭān to kafūrā. Second occurrence of k-w-n in this ayah — now singular, characterizing the archetype.

Form IV imperfect, 2nd person masculine singular, subjunctive with energetic nun (نون التوكيد الثقيلة). Form IV (a'raḍa): causative/factitive of 'araḍa — to make oneself turn sideways, to avert. The energetic nun emphasizes certainty of the action.

Form IV imperfect, 2nd person masculine singular, indicative. Object pronoun -hā refers back to raḥmatin (feminine). Functions as ṣifa (adjective/relative clause) modifying raḥmatin: "a mercy that you hope for." The indicative mood (not subjunctive) within an adjectival clause is standard.

Perfect verb 2mp of kāla/yakīlu (Form I). Despite MASAQ assigning root k-l-l, this is morphologically from k-y-l: the hollow verb kāla (k-y-l) loses its middle radical in the perfect conjugation (kilt-um). Confirms the measuring context established by al-kayla.

Form I imperative 2mp of wazana/yazinu. The imperative zinū commands weighing. MIXED transitivity in the Quran: in 17:35 no explicit direct object (intransitive — "weigh [things]" implied), while 26:182 is identical (also no object). The bi-l-qisṭās phrase specifies the instrument, not the object.
IV imperfect jussive 2ms, apocopated from taqfū. Root q-w-f: to follow, track, step behind.
PV 3ms, defective verb. Here with predicate mas'ūlan. Can read as past (was always), present habitual (is), or prophetic future (will be).
Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive mood (apocopated: tamshi instead of tamshī). Form I. The jussive is governed by lā nāhiya. Root m-sh-y = to walk, to go on foot.
Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb governed by lan). Form I. Root kh-r-q = to tear, pierce, perforate, split, breach.
Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb governed by lan). Form I. Root b-l-gh = to reach, arrive at, attain, convey.

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular. Functions as copula (verb of incomplete predication) with سَيِّئُهُ as subject and مَكْرُوهًا as predicate. Mixed transitivity: here used without external object (copular frame).
Perfect verb, Form IV (af'ala), 3rd person masculine singular; subject is rabbuka (your Lord); the ilayka establishes the recipient; Form IV causative: "caused the waḥy to reach"

Form IV perfect verb (ʾafʿala), 3rd person masculine singular, with 2nd person masculine plural object suffix -kum. Subject is رَبُّكُمْ (word 4). Form IV is causative/transitive of Form I ṣafā (to be pure/clear).

Form VIII perfect verb (iftaʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is رَبُّكُمْ from the first clause. Form VIII of ʾ-kh-dh adds reflexive/deliberate nuance — "to take for oneself, to adopt, to deliberately acquire."
Form I imperfect indicative verb, 2nd person masculine plural; imperfect tense indicates ongoing, habitual speech — a persistent claim, not a one-time utterance

grammar: Form II perfect verb, 1st person plural (majestic "We"). Form II (faʿʿala) is intensive/causative of Form I ṣarafa "to turn." ṣarrafnā = "We turned repeatedly, diversified, varied." Object is deliberately elided — syntactic openness. Transitivity: MIXED (10 with object, 1 without in 18:54). Here no explicit object: either elided (understood as "the message/examples") or used absolutely.

grammar: Form V imperfect verb (tafaʿʿala → yadhdhakkaru, with assimilation of tāʾ into dhāl), 3rd person masculine plural, subjunctive (manṣūb after lām at-taʿlīl). Form V is reflexive of Form II dhakkara "to remind" — so "to remind oneself, to take heed, to recall." Transitivity: MIXED (52 with object, 14 without). Here used intransitively — no explicit object of remembrance.

Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular + attached pronoun -hum (them). Subject is implied — either the Qurʾān (referent of hādhā l-qurʾān) or the act of diversification (ṣarrafnā). Double transitive: increases THEM (object 1) in SOMETHING (object 2, which is nufūran). Transitivity: MIXED (31 with object, 1 without in 3:178). Here fully transitive with two objects.
Form I imperative, 2nd person masculine singular, apocopated (jussive base). Command directed to the Prophet to articulate a logical argument.
Form I perfect, 3rd person masculine singular. Copular/existential verb in the protasis of the counterfactual. Here kāna is existential ("there existed") not copular ("was [something]").

grammar: Form I imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural. Habitual/continuous aspect — they repeatedly make this claim. Subject is the polytheists.
Form VIII perfect, 3rd person masculine plural; ifti'āl pattern adds reflexive/intensive nuance — seeking earnestly for oneself
Perfect verb (PV), Form VI (tafā'ala), 3ms — reflexive: the subject elevates himself; no explicit object; without-object reading attested (17:43, 23:92, 23:116)

Imperfect verb (IV/muḍāri'), Form I, 3mp — active voice, indicative mood (marfū'); subject is the polytheists of prior ayahs (17:40-42); MIXED transitivity: used here without explicit object (content elided — understood from context)

Form II imperfect 3rd masculine singular, indicative mood; subject is implicit shay' (every thing)

Form I perfect, 1st person plural (divine "We"), active voice, transitive — takes double object (ḥijāban + baynaka)

Form I imperative (command verb), 2nd person masculine singular, apocopated (majzūm). Addressed to the Prophet Muhammad. The verb takes kayfa as its complement — an indirect question serving as the object of perception.

Form I perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, active voice. The subject is "they" (the disbelievers). Takes a double object: laka (for you) and al-amthāla (the similitudes). The phrase ḍaraba l-amthāla is a fixed Quranic idiom.

Form I perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, active voice. Used here intransitively (no explicit object) — they themselves went astray (not "they lost something"). The perfect tense marks the straying as a completed fact.

Form X (istaf'ala) imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, indicative mood (marfū'), active voice. Form X of ṭ-w-' typically means "to seek compliance/ability from oneself" — to find within oneself the capacity. The imperfect marks ongoing state. Negated by lā.
perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I, intransitive (no explicit direct object — the quoted speech serves as content)

Form I imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is implicit (mā = whatever). Intransitive here — no direct object. MIXED transitivity: 11 with object, 6 without in IV form group.
Form I imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural, with future particle sa- prefixed. Active voice. 255 Form I imperfect occurrences in Quran — extremely common.

Form IV imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine singular, with 1st person plural object pronoun -nā. Transitive here (with object). MIXED transitivity: 19 with object, 4 without in this form group.
Imperative (command verb), 2nd person masculine singular. Addressed to the Prophet. The kasra on lām is for liaison with following definite article (alladhī).
Form I perfect, 3rd person masculine singular, with 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun -kum. Transitive (with object). MIXED transitivity: 8 with object, 1 without (82:1).

Form IV imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural, with future particle sa-. Transitive (with object ruʾūsahum). This is the ONLY occurrence of this root in the entire Quran (hapax legomenon).

Form I imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural. Active voice. Second occurrence of this verb in the ayah (see word 8 sa-yaqūlūna). Here without sa- prefix — present/habitual rather than explicitly future.
Imperative, 2nd person masculine singular. Second command to the Prophet in this ayah. Apocopated form (qul) — no liaison kasra needed here (followed by ʿasā, not al-).
Form I imperfect subjunctive (manṣūb after an), 3rd person masculine singular. Copulative use (IV_COP). Subject is implied huwa (it/the resurrection). 262 imperfect occurrences in Quran.
Form I imperfect 3rd masculine singular + 2nd masculine plural object suffix -kum; indicative mood
Form X imperfect 2nd masculine plural, indicative mood; istaf'ala pattern = seeking/finding a jawāb (answer)
Form I imperfect 2nd masculine plural, indicative mood; doubled final radical (nūn)
Form I perfect 2nd masculine plural; lām assimilated with preceding in (shadda on lām)

Form I imperative (amr), 2nd person masculine singular. Addressed to the Prophet. Command verb introducing reported speech. The imperative is apocopated (shortened from qul, base q-w-l with medial wāw elided in imperative).

Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, jussive mood (majzūm). The jussive here functions as an indirect command: qul lahum yaqūlū = say to them, let them say. The deletion of the nūn (from yaqūlūna → yaqūlū) marks the jussive.

Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative mood (marfūʿ). Subject is ash-shayṭān. The verb n-z-gh means to prick, to provoke, to incite discord. Note: the bundle lists root as ن ز ع (n-z-') but the actual verb form here is يَنْزَغُ with غ (ghayn), from root n-z-gh. The MASAQ mapping uses n-z-' as an approximation.

Form I perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is ash-shayṭān. kāna here functions as a copular verb establishing the predicate (ʿaduwwan mubīnā) for its subject. The perfect tense with kāna often indicates a permanent/essential state rather than past action.
Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive (apocopated) — jazm by in conditional; Form I
notes: object_omitted_after_will

grammar: Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive (apocopated as jawāb al-sharṭ); Form I; transitive with attached pronoun -kum as direct object
Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive (apocopated); Form I; second occurrence — identical form to word 5
notes: object_omitted_after_will

grammar: Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive (apocopated as jawāb al-sharṭ); Form II (causative/intensive); transitive with -kum as direct object
Perfect verb, 1st person plural (majestic We), Form IV (af'ala); transitive with -ka as direct object; indicates completed divine action of sending
perfect verb, Form II (fa''ala), 1st person plural (divine 'We'), transitive with 'alā
perfect verb, Form IV (af'ala), 1st person plural (divine 'We'), transitive (double object: dāwūda + zabūran)

Form I imperative, 2nd person masculine plural, from root d-'-' meaning to call/invoke/summon
Form I perfect, 2nd person masculine plural, with explicit -tum suffix marking the addressees
Form I imperfect, 3rd person masculine plural, active voice, indicative mood — transitive, object is kashfa

Imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I; subject ambiguous -- either the human worshippers (they call upon [others]) or the invoked beings (they call out [to God]); no explicit object present in ayah

Imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural, Form VIII (iftiʿāl pattern); reflexive-intensive of b-gh-y; subject = either the invoked beings or the callers depending on parsing; object = al-wasīlata
Imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I; transitive with direct object raḥmatahu; subject = the invoked beings or the callers
Imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I; transitive with direct object ʿadhābahu; subject = same as yarjūna
Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I; copular verb establishing a permanent state (kāna + predicate = perpetual characterization); subject = ʿadhāba rabbika (via inna construction)

Perfect tense verb (PV), 3rd person masculine singular. Here used as kāna al-sha'niyyah (existential kāna) — establishing a timeless truth rather than past narrative. Subject: dhālika. Predicate: masṭūran.
PV — perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine singular with 1st person plural pronoun suffix -nā (Us); transitive, taking two objects: the implied divine subject and the maṣdar clause an nursila
IV subjunctive — Form IV (arsala/yursilu), 1st person plural, subjunctive mood (mansūb by an); the Form IV causative means "to cause to be sent, to dispatch, to commission"

PV — perfect verb, Form II (fa''ala), 3rd person masculine singular; the doubling (tashīd) of the middle radical intensifies the meaning from "to lie" (Form I) to "to declare/call a liar, to deny as lies"
