grammar: PV — perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine plural; the root z-l-m originally means "to place in darkness" and extends to "to wrong, to be unjust, to oppress"
notes: direct_object_omitted

grammar: IV indicative — Form IV, 1st person plural, indicative mood (marfū'); the shift from subjunctive nursila (v.59a) to indicative nursilu marks the change from hypothetical past to ongoing present-tense policy
PV — perfect verb, 1st person plural (royal We), Form I; the root q-w-l means to say/speak/declare; MASAQ assigns q-l-l but the verb is from q-w-l (hollow root)
PV — perfect verb, Form IV (af'ala), 3rd person masculine singular; causative of h-w-t; transitive with bi-
PV — perfect verb, Form I, 1st person plural; ja'ala = to make, to render, to appoint, to design; takes double object: ru'yā (1st object) + fitnatan (2nd object)
object_roots: ر أ ي;ف ت ن;ش ج ر

grammar: IV — Form IV perfect (af'ala pattern), 1st person plural with 2nd person singular object suffix -ka; causative: to cause someone to see, to show, to reveal to
Form II imperfect, 1p, indicative, with 3mp object pronoun -hum; causative/intensive — to cause fear, to frighten repeatedly; divine "We" as subject
Imperfect verb, 3ms, indicative, Form I, with 3mp object pronoun -hum; subject is the implied "it" (the warning/frightening); takes ṭughyānan as second object (tamyīz)
PV, perfect verb, 1st person plural (divine "We"), Form I; introduces direct speech (the command to prostrate)
CV, command verb (imperative), 2nd person masculine plural, Form I; direct command from God to the angels
PV, perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I; reports the angels' compliance with the command
PV, perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I; introduces Iblis' direct speech

Interrogative hamza (hamzat al-istifhām) prefixed to Form I imperfect verb, 1st person singular; rhetorical question expressing incredulity and refusal; Iblis questions the divine command to prostrate
PV, perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, Form I; Iblis addresses God directly as creator
PV, perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I; introduces Iblis' direct speech following the prostration narrative of 17:61

PV, perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular with appended كَ (kāf al-khiṭāb, address particle); interrogative أ- prefix; from root r-'-y (seeing/perceiving); the -ka suffix is NOT a pronoun object but an intensifying address particle
PV, perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, Form II (intensive/causative); transitive with implied object (هَٰذَا / Adam); the Form II intensification signals deliberate, elevated honoring
PV, perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, Form II (intensive); with 1st person singular object suffix -nī; transitive — God is the agent, Iblis is the patient of the delaying
Form VIII (iftaʿala) imperfect, 1st person singular, energetic mood with the heavy nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla; the only Quranic occurrence of this root
PV, perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I; introduces God's direct speech responding to Iblis' threat in 17:62
CV, imperative verb, 2nd person masculine singular, Form I; bare imperative with no stated destination or object; functions as a dismissal granting Iblis his requested respite implicitly
PV, perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, Form I; transitive with attached 2ms pronoun -ka (object = Iblis); perfect tense in conditional clause expresses future certainty
Form X imperative, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive (apocopated), transitive with direct object (man)
Form X perfect, 2nd person masculine singular, active voice
Form IV imperative, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive, transitive (with 'alayhim as prepositional complement)
Form III imperative, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive, transitive with direct object -hum, + fī prepositional complement
imperative, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive, transitive with direct object -hum
Form IV imperfect, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative, transitive with direct object -hum
Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular; the bā' in bi-rabbika introduces the real subject (fā'il) — kafā bi-rabbika = "sufficient is your Lord"
Form IV imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative (marfū'), active voice
Form VIII (iftaʿala) imperfect subjunctive (manṣūb by the lām), 2nd person masculine plural, active voice — reflexive seeking
Perfect tense verb (fi'l māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular, active voice, copulative
PV (perfect verb), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular with 2nd person masculine plural object suffix -kum; subject follows (ḍurr)
PV (perfect verb), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, subject is man (the one whom you call)
IV (imperfect verb), Form I, 2nd person masculine plural, active voice; expressing ongoing habitual calling
PV (perfect verb), Form II (intensive/causative), 3rd person masculine singular with 2nd person masculine plural object suffix -kum; subject is God (implied)
PV (perfect verb), Form IV (af'ala), 2nd person masculine plural, active; intransitive usage (no direct object)
PV (perfect verb), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular; copula establishing permanent characterization

Perfect verb (PV), 2nd person masculine plural. Form I amina: to be safe, to feel secure, to trust. The perfect tense indicates the addressees have already entered a state of assumed security. Subject: implicit 2nd person plural (those rescued from the sea).

Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb by an). The subject is God (implicit). The bi- in bikum marks the affected party, and jāniba l-barri is the direct object (the thing caused to sink). Alternatively, bikum can be read as the object of swallowing (He sinks you).

Form IV imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb, governed by an from earlier). IV causative: to send, to dispatch, to release. Subject is God (implicit). Object is ḥāṣiban (stone-storm). The verb is complemented by ʿalaykum (upon you).

Form I imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural, subjunctive/jussive (the form is ambiguous here; contextually subjunctive in result clause after thumma lā). From j-d-d: to find, to discover, to encounter. Subject: the addressees. Object: wakīlā.
Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural; from '-m-n "to be secure, to trust, to believe." Used here in the interrogative (preceded by am) to challenge the addressees' sense of safety.

Form IV imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive (manṣūb by an), with 2nd person masculine plural object pronoun -kum. Form IV (af'ala/yu'īdu) = causative of '-w-d: "to cause to return, to restore, to send back."
Form IV imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive (governed by an via fa). From r-s-l: "to send, to dispatch, to release." Form IV = causative: "to cause to be sent."
Form IV imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, subjunctive (an-chain via fa), with 2mp object pronoun -kum. Form IV (aghraq/yughriqu) = causative of gh-r-q: "to cause to drown."
Perfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural, from k-f-r. The only verb in the ayah addressed directly to the second person (the others are third person or subjunctive descriptions of divine action).

Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine plural, from j-d-d (wajada/yajidu). The initial wāw of the root drops in the imperfect. Subjunctive form (loss of final nūn: tajidū instead of tajidūna) — context may govern this through an implied an after thumma.

Perfect verb, Form II (فَعَّلَ), 1st person plural (majestic "We"), transitive. Form II of k-r-m adds intensive/causative force: not merely "was generous" but "actively conferred dignity/nobility upon." Direct object: بَنِىٓ ءَادَمَ.

Perfect verb, Form I, 1st person plural + 3rd person masculine plural object suffix (-hum). Transitive: "We carried them." The -hum refers back to banī Ādam. h-m-l denotes bearing weight — physical, moral, or intellectual burden.
Perfect verb, Form I, 1st person plural + 3rd person masculine plural object suffix (-hum). Transitive: "We provided/sustained them." Governs partitive مِنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ.

Perfect verb, Form II (فَعَّلَ), 1st person plural + 3rd person masculine plural object suffix (-hum). Transitive: "We gave them surplus/preference." Form II intensive: not mere surplus but deliberate, emphatic preferring. Governs عَلَىٰ كَثِيرٍ (preferred over many).

Perfect verb, Form I, 1st person plural (majestic "We"). Intransitive in this clause (no explicit object — object is implied "what/all things"). kh-l-q denotes originating from nothing, creating, fashioning; also: fabricating, lying.
Imperfect indicative, 1st person plural — majestic "We" (God speaking). Transitive verb taking kulla unāsin as direct object. Imperfect tense for a future event gives vividness (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl).

Perfect passive (Form IV — u'ṭiya/ūtiya). Subject is the implicit "whoever" (man). The passive obscures the giver — deliberately leaving divine agency implicit rather than explicit. kitābahū is the direct object retained in the passive construction (maf'ūl thānī).
notes: passive with retained accusative complement

grammar: Imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural active. Subject is ulā'ika (those). Transitive verb taking kitābahum as direct object. Imperfect tense for a future event — narrative vividness (as with nad'ū).

Imperfect passive indicative, 3rd person masculine plural. Subject is the implicit "they" (= ulā'ika, the right-hand recipients). Passive voice — they are not subjected to any wronging/diminishing. The fatīlā that follows is a tamyīz (specification of extent).
Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; kopulative verb establishing a state; here in conditional protasis governed by man
Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural; verb of approximation (af'āl al-muqāraba) indicating near-completion of an action that did not occur
Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural with 2nd person singular object suffix -ka; Form I active — the subject acts upon the addressee; khabar of kādū
Perfect verb, 1st person plural (royal We); Form IV (af'ala); direct revelation from God; object is implicit (alladhī = what We revealed)
Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb by lām); Form VIII (iftarā) — reflexive fabrication
Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural with 2nd person singular object -ka; Form VIII (ittakhadha); double accusative verb — takes two objects (you + khalīlā)
Form II perfect, 1st person plural + 2nd person masculine singular object suffix -ka
perfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, from kāda (verb of proximity)
Form I imperfect, 2nd person masculine singular, indicative (marfūʿ)
notes: رَكَنَ governs its target with إِلَى

grammar: Form IV (causative) perfect verb adhāqa, 1st person plural subject (-nā) with 2nd person masculine singular object suffix (-ka); causative "to make taste / cause to experience"

Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, Form I. From the root w-j-d (to find). In the conditional apodosis context, functions as a hypothetical: you would not find. Takes laka as indirect object (for yourself), ʿalaynā as prepositional complement (against Us), and naṣīran as direct object.

Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, from kāda/yakādu (an auxiliary verb of approximation). Functions as a near-completion auxiliary: the action described in the following imperfect verb almost occurred but did not. Subject is the adversarial group (referenced from context).

Form X imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural + 2nd person masculine singular object pronoun -ka; istafʿala — seeking/causing the base meaning of agitation/trembling to be applied to the addressee

Form IV imperfect subjunctive verb, 3rd person masculine plural + 2nd person masculine singular object -ka; subjunctive (manṣūb, dropped nūn) governed by lām al-taʿlīl; akhraja = causative of kharaja (to go out) = to cause to go out

Form I imperfect, 3rd person masculine plural, indicative mood. From labitha/yalbathu (to stay, to remain, to linger). Subject is the adversarial group. After idhan + lā, creates counterfactual: they would not have stayed.
Perfect verb, Form IV (af'ala), first person plural (royal We/divine plural), active voice; from root r-s-l; takes implicit object (man = those whom)

Imperfect verb, Form IV (af'ala, though classical wajada behaves irregularly), second person singular masculine, active voice, indicative mood (marfu'); takes tahwilan as direct object and li-sunnatina as prepositional complement
Form IV imperative, 2nd person masculine singular; commands the addressee to cause ṣalāt to stand/be established; the kasra on mīm is liaison vowel before lām of the next word
Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular; copular use as predicate of inna-clause; kāna here indicates a permanent/timeless state, not past tense
Form V (tafaʿʿul) imperative, 2nd person masculine singular, active; from hajada — the only Quranic occurrence of this root
Form I imperfect (yafʿalu), subjunctive (after أَنْ), 3rd person masculine singular, active, with attached pronoun كَ (2ms object); subject is رَبُّكَ
notes: مَقَامًا also has an adverbial parse

grammar: Form I imperative, 2nd person masculine singular. Command to speak, addressed to the Prophet or any reader. The verb governs everything that follows as direct speech.

Form IV imperative (apocopated), 2nd person masculine singular with 1st person object suffix -nī. From dakhala (I, to enter). The Form IV (af'ala) makes it causative: to cause entry, to make enter, to admit.

Form IV imperative (apocopated), 2nd person masculine singular with 1st person object suffix -nī. From kharaja (I, to go out). The Form IV makes it causative: to cause to exit, to bring out, to extract.
Form I imperative (apocopated), 2nd person masculine singular. Takes double accusative: lī (for me) as indirect beneficiary, and sulṭānan naṣīran as the thing made/granted. Transitive.
Imperative (CV), 2nd person masculine singular, Form I, apocopated (jazm); from q-w-l "to say"
Perfect verb (PV), 3rd person masculine singular, Form I, active; intransitive in this ayah (no explicit object)
Perfect verb (PV), 3rd person masculine singular, Form I, active, intransitive
Perfect verb (PV), 3rd person masculine singular, Form I, active; incomplete/copular verb (kāna nāqiṣa) taking predicate zahūqā
Form II imperfect, 1st person plural, active, indicative (marfūʿ)
Form I imperfect, 3rd person masculine singular, active, indicative (marfūʿ)
Form IV perfect, 1st person plural (divine We), transitive with ʿalā
Form IV perfect, 3rd person masculine singular, intransitive (no explicit object here)
Form I perfect, 3rd person masculine singular, intransitive with bi- (instrumental)
Form I perfect, 3rd person masculine singular + 3ms object pronoun (-hu), transitive
Form I perfect, 3rd person masculine singular, copular verb introducing predicate (yaʾūsan)
Form I imperative (jussive-apocopated), 2nd person masculine singular, addressing the Prophet

grammar: Form I imperfect indicative 3mp + 2ms object suffix -ka, yasʾalūna-ka

grammar: Perfect verb, 1st person plural. Root sh-y-' Form I. Subject is divine (royal We). No explicit object — used absolutely here.
notes: شِئْنَا is used absolutely in the conditional formula

grammar: Imperfect verb, 1st person plural, Form I, with nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla (heavy emphasis nūn). The بِ (bi-) that follows governs the object — dh-h-b bi-shay' = to take away/remove something.
Perfect verb, 1st person plural, Form IV (af'ala). Root w-h-y. Subject: divine (We). Form IV adds causative/transitive force: to cause waḥy to reach someone.
notes: The relative head supplies the revealed content outside an explicit object slot

grammar: Imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, Form I. Root w-j-d. Note: the bundle assigns root j-d-d, but the standard root for wajada/yajidu is و ج د (w-j-d). MASAQ's j-d-d assignment reflects the surface stem جد without the initial wāw.

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī); third-person masculine singular; functions as copula (verb of incomplete predication — kāna nāqiṣa); its subject is faḍluhū (via inna construction); its predicate is kabīrā; kāna here does not indicate past tense but established/permanent state
Form I imperative verb, 2nd person masculine singular. Apocopated (majzūm) imperative form of qāla. Addressed to the Prophet as the commanded speaker.

Form VIII perfect verb (ifta'ala pattern), 3rd person feminine singular. The tāʾ al-taʾnīth agrees with al-insu (feminine in form as a collective noun). Form VIII adds reflexive/mutual meaning to the base: gathered themselves, came together mutually.

Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, subjunctive (manṣūb by an; the wāw is dropped in subjunctive: yaʾtūna → yaʾtū). Subject is al-ins wa-l-jinn. Used here intransitively with bi- (yaʾtū bi- = to bring, to produce, to come with).

Form I imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, indicative (marfūʿ). Unlike yaʾtū in word 9 (subjunctive = attempt), this is indicative (= factual assertion of failure). Subject is the same ins + jinn. The -na ending confirms indicative mood.
Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. Copular verb (filler/auxiliary) introducing the predicate ẓahīran. Subject is baʿḍuhum. Here in the counterfactual past (law kāna = "even if [it] were").

Form II perfect verb, 1st person plural (divine "We"). Form II (faʿʿala) is intensive/frequentative of Form I ṣarafa (to turn). The doubling of the middle radical signals repeated, intensive action. Subject is God (implied in -nā). Direct object is elided.

Form I perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is aktharu (most). The alif maqṣūra ending indicates a lām-alif verb (defective verb). Transitive verb whose object is elided -- what they refused is implied (acceptance/belief). The exception clause illā kufūran paradoxically fills the gap.
Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), 3rd person masculine plural. Reports completed speech. The plural subject refers to the Meccan disbelievers (contextually established). The wāw al-jamā'a marks plural agent.

Form IV imperfect verb (af'ala pattern), 1st person plural, subjunctive mood (manṣūb after lan). Form IV is causative/estimative: "to make safe / to consider safe / to place trust." The lām preposition after it (laka) marks the person toward whom trust is directed.

Form I imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, subjunctive mood (manṣūb after ḥattā). From f-j-r: to split open, to cleave, to burst forth. The subject is the Prophet (you). Takes yanbū'an as its object. The demand is for the Prophet to personally perform the act of splitting.
Form I imperfect subjunctive 2nd masculine singular (mansūb by aw continuing ḥattā from 17:90)
Form II imperfect subjunctive 2nd masculine singular (mansūb by fa following aw + subjunctive chain)
Form IV imperfect subjunctive (mansub), 2nd person masculine singular active; causative of s-q-t (to fall) — you cause falling; subjunctive mood governed by أَنْ from preceding context
perfect verb (PV), 2nd person masculine singular active; from z-'-m — to claim, allege, assert; perfect tense = completed claim in the past that is now being held against the claimant
Form IV imperfect subjunctive (mansub), 2nd person masculine singular active; from '-t-y (to come, to bring); with بِ (bi) = to bring, to come with; subjunctive governed by preceding أَنْ
Form I imperfect subjunctive 3rd masculine singular, copulative (IV_COP in MASAQ); subjunctive because of أَوْ continuing the ḥattā chain from 17:90
Form I imperfect subjunctive 2nd masculine singular; intransitive here (ascending without stated destination-object)
Form IV imperfect subjunctive 1st plural; governed by لَن; transitive here with لِ marking the topic of belief
Form II imperfect subjunctive 2nd masculine singular; causative intensive — causing something to descend repeatedly or thoroughly
Form I imperfect indicative 1st plural + 3rd masculine singular object pronoun هُ; relative clause modifying kitāban (implied alladhī)
Form I imperative 2nd masculine singular; divine command to the Prophet to respond; apocopated form
Form I perfect 1st singular; existential/copulative; kāna + tā' al-mutakallim; past tense asserting an established state
Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, active voice. Transitive — takes double accusative: النَّاسَ (direct object) + أَن يُؤْمِنُوا (second object/clausal complement).
Imperfect verb (IV), Form IV (أَفْعَلَ), 3rd person masculine plural, subjunctive mood (after أَن). Form IV causative: to cause oneself to enter security, to entrust, to believe.
Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular with attached pronoun هُمُ (3rd masc. pl., accusative). Subject: الهدى (guidance). Transitive — the pronoun is the direct object.
Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine plural. Introduces direct speech (the objection). Subject: implied "they" (the people, النَّاس from earlier).
Interrogative hamza أَ + perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. The hamza al-istifhām introduces a rhetorical question expressing incredulity. Subject: اللَّهُ.
Form I imperative 2nd masculine singular; command verb addressed to the Prophet; apocopated (jazm) imperative form
Form I perfect 3rd masculine singular; copulative verb in counterfactual protasis; subject is malā'ikatun (feminine plural but kāna takes masculine for broken plurals)
Form I imperfect indicative 3rd masculine plural; ḥāl (circumstantial clause) describing the state of malā'ika; agrees with masculine plural for non-human broken plural

Emphatic lām al-jawāb prefixed to Form II perfect 1st plural nazzalnā; apodosis of law-conditional; intensive/causative of n-z-l with divine "We" subject; Form II implies gradual/phased sending down (vs. Form IV anzala for single act)
Form I imperative (command verb), 2ms, apocopated (jussive base), addressed to the Prophet
Form I perfect verb, 3ms; in kafā bi-X construction, the bāʾ introduces the actual subject (Allāh); MIXED transitivity (16 with object, 11 without)
notes: formulaic kafā bi construction

grammar: Form I perfect verb, 3ms; functions as kāna al-nāqiṣa (defective/incomplete verb) introducing predicate adjectives; MIXED transitivity (773 with object, 297 without)

Imperfect verb (fiʿl muḍāriʿ), 2nd person masculine plural. Form I. Root ʿ-b-d encompasses worship, servitude, and enslavement. The imperfect tense marks the action as habitual and ongoing — "what do you keep worshipping?" — questioning an entrenched practice. The plural -ūna addresses both the father and the people collectively.

Perfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, Form I. Introduces direct speech. The wāw suffix marks plural subject. The preceding context (26:70) has Abraham asking "What do you worship?" — qālū is the responsive speech-act.

Imperfect verb, 1st person plural, Form I. Indicative mood (marfūʿ, -u ending). Takes aṣnāman as direct object. The imperfect conveys ongoing, habitual action — this is not a one-time act but a continuous state of worship.

Imperfect verb, 1st person plural, Form I. Copular/auxiliary use: naẓallu + predicate (ʿākifīna) = "we remain/continue being devoted." Classical Arabic: ẓalla specifically means "to be in a state during the daytime" (one of the kāna-and-sisters group: kāna, aṣbaḥa, amsā, ẓalla, bāta, etc.). The geminate root (ẓ-l-l) produces the doubled lām in naẓallu.

Form IV (afʿala) imperfect active, 3rd person masculine plural. From f-s-d: root meaning to be bad, spoiled, corrupt, rotten. Form IV (afsada) is causative: "to cause to be corrupt/ruined." The Form IV is significant: the musrifīn are not merely corrupt (passive: fasadū) but are causing corruption (causative: yufsidūna) — their agency produces fasād in others and in the environment. ROOT_LEXICON: 180 Quranic occurrences; very_common tier; IV:8 (MIXED: 6 obj / 2 no_obj); NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:136 (dominant form, the muṣliḥ/ūn and ṣāliḥ/ūn); GERUND:9; CV:6; PV:16. The imperfect (yuṣliḥūna), negated by lā, states the factual absence of the musrifīn's restorative action. The Form IV is causative, paralleling the Form IV of f-s-d: just as yufsidūna = they cause corruption (causative), yuṣliḥūna would mean = they cause soundness/repair; lā yuṣliḥūna = they cause no repair.

grammar: Verb: perfect active (PV), 3rd person masculine plural. From q-w-l: "to say, speak, state, utter." The PV 3MP form qālū is the standard reporting formula for speech acts in Quranic narrative, and in S26 it appears repeatedly to introduce community responses to prophets. The full form would be qawalū, contracted to qālū (wāw of the root fuses with the connecting vowel: q-ā-l-ū). The verb takes the following direct speech as its content — no bi or li-intermediary, direct quotation structure. In this context, qālū introduces not an individual retort but a communal pronouncement: the subject is Thamūd as a community (or their spokesmen/leaders), making this a formal collective speech act of rejection.

Verb: Form IV (afʿala) imperative (amr), second person masculine singular, apocopated (jussive-like short form of the imperative). From ʾ-t-y: "to come, to arrive, to bring." Governs the prepositional object bi-āyatin. In Quranic usage, ʾti bi- + āya is the standard formula for demanding a divine sign: "produce a miracle as evidence." The command issues the formal challenge to provide the extraordinary demonstration that would prove divine backing.

grammar: Verb: kāna (Form I perfect/PV), second person masculine singular. From k-w-n: "to be, to exist." ROOT_LEXICON: 1,396 Quranic occurrences; PV: 1,070 (dominant). Kunta is the past tense form (kunta = you were/you are, the PV 2ms), functioning here within the conditional in-kunta as a stative present: "if you are [currently] of the truthful." Kāna in conditional protases often functions as a timeless stative rather than a past-tense claim — "if you are [and have been] truthful." This is standard Quranic usage: in kunta mina l-ṣādiqīn = "if you are [indeed, really] of the truthful ones."

Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. From q-w-l: "to say, speak, utter." ROOT_LEXICON: 1337 Quranic occurrences, dominant form PV:911. Form I imperfect active, jussive (majzūm), 2nd person masculine plural + hā (feminine 3rd person object suffix). From m-s-s: "to touch, to handle, to come into contact with." ROOT_LEXICON: 61 Quranic occurrences; IV:30 (dominant verbal form); PV:28; TRANSITIVITY: MIXED (27 obj / 3 no_obj). The base sense is physical contact — touching as the most basic form of physical interaction. The jussive here is governed by lā al-nāhiya; the hā suffix refers to the she-camel (nāqa, feminine) established in the surrounding context. The verb does not specify the nature of the touching until the prepositional phrase bi-sūʾin — tamassūhā by itself is neutral (touching), but bi-sūʾin specifies the forbidden mode.

Form I imperfect active, subjunctive (manṣūb, governed by fa al-sababiyya), 3rd person masculine singular + kum (2nd person masculine plural object suffix). From ʾ-kh-dh: "to take, seize, grasp, apprehend." ROOT_LEXICON: 273 Quranic occurrences; IV:89; PV:142; TRANSITIVITY: IV TRANS (MIXED: 50obj/3no_obj); PV MIXED (140obj/2no_obj). The 3ms form has ʿadhābu yawmin ʿaẓīmin as its subject (punishment seizes you); the kum suffix marks the addressee community (all of Thamūd) as the object of the seizing. The root ʾ-kh-dh in the Quran carries the sense of sudden, comprehensive divine apprehension — God "takes" sinful nations suddenly and totally.

Form I perfect active (PV), third person masculine plural, with attached direct object pronoun -hā (her, referring to the she-camel, al-nāqa Allāh of v.155). ROOT_LEXICON: 8 Quranic occurrences; PV:5; NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:3; TRANSITIVITY PV:TRANS. The root ʿ-q-r denotes cutting or wounding the hocks/hind tendons of an animal to immobilize it — the standard pre-slaughter technique for large animals in antiquity. In Quranic usage, ʿaqara al-nāqa (to hamstring the she-camel) is the specific transgression associated with Thamūd across multiple surahs (7:77, 11:65, 26:157, 54:29, 91:14). The plural ʿaqarūhā assigns collective responsibility to the whole community — not one individual but all of Thamūd.

Form IV perfect active (PV), third person masculine plural. From ṣ-b-ḥ: "to reach morning, to begin the day; to become, to enter into a state." ROOT_LEXICON: 43 Quranic occurrences; PV:22 dominant; MIXED transitivity (19 obj / 3 no_obj). Functions here as a kāna-type verb (fiʿl nāqiṣ) with nādimīna as its khabar (predicate nominative): "they became regretful." The Form IV aṣbaḥa (IV of ṣ-b-ḥ) adds the temporal sense of morning to the state-change: the state was entered at morning, or the state was entered with the arrival of a new condition (the completion of the act). The co-occurrence pattern with n-d-m (top co-occ ṣ-b-ḥ with ن د م: 5 times) confirms that aṣbaḥa + nādimīna is a fixed Quranic formula for post-transgression remorse.

Verb (fiʿl māḍī / PV), 3rd masculine singular perfect active, Form I; with attached 3mp object suffix -hum; root ʾ-kh-dh = to take, seize, grasp, capture; here the subject (fāʿil) follows the verb: al-ʿadhābu; direct object: -hum (Thamūd)
Verb (fiʿl māḍī / PV), 3rd masculine singular perfect, copular function; ism kāna = aktharuhum (nominative), khabar kāna = muʾminīna (accusative)
PV.3FS — perfect verb, 3rd person feminine singular, Form II (faʿʿala), intensive/factitive; feminine tāʾ in agreement with collective noun qawm

Perfect tense verb (PV), Form I (qaʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. ROOT_LEXICON: 1337 Quranic occurrences; PV:911 — qāla is the most common single verb form in the Quran. ROOT q-w-l: to say, speak, utter; the primary verb of reported speech. Here qāla introduces Lūṭ's direct speech (the refrain a-lā tattaqūna), which is its object. The subject of qāla is akhūhum Lūṭun (deferred subject, coming after the verb — VSO word order, normal in Arabic). The simple past (qāla = he said) places the speech in historical past time, consistent with idh (when).

Verb, Form VIII (iftaʿala pattern), imperfect active indicative, 2nd person masculine plural — "you (pl.) fear/protect yourselves." ROOT w-q-y: to shield, protect, guard from harm; Form VIII ittaqā: to guard oneself, to be God-conscious, to have taqwā. ROOT_LEXICON: 256 Quranic occurrences; IV:59 (Form IV), NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:52, CV:92 — the root is very_common, appearing across multiple forms. The -ūna ending marks indicative mood, 2mp. In the refrain a-lā tattaqūna, the verb bears the full semantic weight of taqwā: God-consciousness, self-restraint, protective fear, reverence, and compliance with divine limits. The root produces the fundamental Islamic concept taqwā (piety/God-consciousness) as its gerund.
notes: object of fearing is unexpressed

grammar: Imperative (CV), Form VIII (iftaʿala), second person masculine plural. From w-q-y: "to protect, guard, shield." Form VIII reflexive: "protect oneself, guard oneself through God." Direct object: Allāha (accusative). ROOT_LEXICON: 256 Quranic occurrences; 92 CV; MIXED transitivity (90 obj / 2 no_obj). The command is addressed to the people of Lūṭ, whose defining characteristic in this pericope is transgressive approach (v.165: taʾtūna al-dhukrān) — the command to "shield yourselves through God" redirects the energy of transgressive-approach toward protective-God-consciousness.

Imperative (CV), Form IV (afʿala), second person masculine plural + nūn al-wiqāya + first-person singular pronoun (-nī contracted to -ni before pause). From ṭ-w-ʿ: "to obey, comply voluntarily." ROOT_LEXICON: 128 Quranic occurrences; 31 CV; 53 IV. MIXED transitivity (50 obj / 3 no_obj). Form IV is the standard Quranic directed-obedience form. The nūn al-wiqāya protects the final vowel before the pronoun suffix. In the Lūṭ pericope, aṭīʿūni commands obedience specifically to Lūṭ — the messenger who is precisely being threatened with expulsion (v.167: "If you do not desist, O Lūṭ, you will surely be among the expelled").

Imperfect verb (muḍāriʿ), Form I, 1st person singular, active. Direct object: -kum (you, plural, referring to Lūṭ's people). The verb s-ʾ-l governs two objects: the person asked (kum) and the thing asked for (ajr, negated by mā...min). IV:MIXED transitivity — 54 with object, 11 without. 128 total occurrences in Quran.

IV 2nd person masculine plural imperfect with prefixed hamza al-istifhām (interrogative/condemnation particle); Form I; transitive here with al-dhukrāna as direct object. Root ʾ-t-y: COUNT 544, TIER very_common; IV:217 (MIXED: 204 obj / 13 no_obj). The base meaning is directed motion toward a destination or person.

Imperfect active, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. ROOT_LEXICON: 84 occurrences; IV:24, CV:22; MIXED transitivity (23 obj / 1 no_obj). The verb dhaara/yadhaaru (w-dh-r, Form I) means "to leave, abandon, forsake" — it is transitive here with mā (what your Lord created for you) as the direct object. The imperfect tense makes the abandonment ongoing and habitual, not a one-time act. W-dh-r appears in Quranic contexts of abandoning what should be maintained (e.g., legal obligations, proper relations); here the object of abandonment is divinely-provisioned — making the habitual forsaking a sustained refusal of God's provision.

Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. ROOT_LEXICON: 261 occurrences; very_common; PV:152 (dominant); TRANSITIVITY: PV MIXED (143 obj / 9 no_obj). Subject (fāʿil): rabbukum (your Lord). Object: mā (relative pronoun = "what"). The verb khalaqa here places the act of creation squarely in the divine register: God, as the people's own Lord (rabbukum), is the creator of the mates they are abandoning. The choice of khalaqa (creation ex nihilo / fashioning) rather than jaʿala (making/appointing) or razaqa (providing/sustaining) emphasizes the ontological ground: these mates are part of the divine creation-order, not merely a social custom or preference.

IV energetic 2MS — Form I imperfect verb, second person masculine singular, energetic mood (nūn al-tawkīd al-thaqīla); pro-drop subject = Lūṭ

Perfective verb (PV), Form I (faʿala), third person masculine singular. From q-w-l: "to say, speak, utter." ROOT_LEXICON: 1337 occurrences, 911 PV, MIXED transitivity (726 obj / 185 no_obj). Here qāla introduces Lot's direct speech — the reporting verb that frames the nominal clause of vv.168 as Lot's utterance. In the Lot pericope of S26, every speech act of Lot is introduced by qāla (v.161: qāla lahum akhūhum Lūṭun, v.168: qāla), maintaining the formal narrative structure. At v.168, the reporting verb is stripped of its addressee (no "to them" or "to his people") — Lot's declaration of loathing is framed as absolute, not addressed to a specified recipient.

Verb, Form II imperative active, second person masculine singular, with first person singular object suffix -nī. Form II of n-j-w: najjā/yunajjī = to rescue completely, to deliver fully. The gemination (shaddah on jīm: najji-) is the Form II marker; the imperative drops the ta- prefix; the suffix -nī = first person singular object "me." ROOT_LEXICON: 84 Quranic occurrences; CV:7, GERUND:10, IV:14, NOUN_ABSTRACT:2, NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:3, PV:45, PV_PASS:1; tier common; confidence opus-verified. TRANSITIVITY: CV:TRANS. Top co-occurrences: ʾ-l-h (19), k-w-n (19), q-w-m (15), ʾ-m-n (15), q-w-l (13). N-j-w's base sense is escape/deliverance: najā (I) = to escape, be saved; anjā (IV) = to save (causative); najjā (II) = to save thoroughly/completely (intensive). The CV (Form II) 7 occurrences include direct imperatives and jussives addressed to God — najjinā, najjinī. The Form II (rather than IV anjā) intensifies the rescue: najjā conveys complete, thorough deliverance.

Verb, Form I imperfect active indicative, third person masculine plural (yafʿalūna pattern). From ʿ-m-l: "to do, work, act, produce (deeds)." ROOT_LEXICON: 360 Quranic occurrences; IV:166, PV:99, GERUND:32, NOUN_ABSTRACT:39, NOUN_ACTIVE_PART:13, CV:11; tier very_common; confidence verified. TRANSITIVITY: IV:MIXED (138 obj / 28 no_obj). Top co-occurrences: ʾ-l-h (141), k-w-n (111), ʾ-m-n (101), ṣ-l-ḥ (93), r-b-b (51). Form I yaʿmalu/yaʿmalūna is the standard Quranic form for "they do" — the general deed-production verb without Form IV's directive connotation. The imperfect (mudāriʿ) marks the action as present/ongoing at the moment of Lot's prayer: they are currently doing this. The third person plural (hum) refers to qawm Lūṭ — the people Lot has been addressing in the pericope (the masculine plural subject). The object of yaʿmalūna is implicit/deleted (ma is the relativizer that points to their deeds as a class): "the things they are doing."

Perfect verb (PV), Form II (faʿʿala → najjā → najjaynā), 1st person plural (divine "We") + 3rd masculine singular object pronoun -hu (referring to Lūṭ). ROOT_LEXICON: 84 Quranic occurrences; PV:45; TRANSITIVITY: PV:TRANS. Form II (najjā) intensifies the base Form I (najā = to escape) — the intensive form of the root signals emphatic, thorough, or completed deliverance. The object pronoun -hu is Lūṭ, the individual prophet; the coordinated second object (wa-ahlahu) extends the rescue to his family. The Form II distinguishes this rescue from the Form IV (anjā) used in 26:119 and 26:65 — a deliberate lexical choice within the same root's derivational paradigm.

Verb: Form II (faʿʿala pattern: dammara), perfect tense, active voice, 1st person plural (majestic/royal we — naḥnu, the divine). From root d-m-r: to destroy, to annihilate, to obliterate. ROOT_LEXICON: COUNT:10, TIER:uncommon, CONFIDENCE:verified. FORMS: GERUND:2, IV:1, PV:7. TRANSITIVITY: IV:TRANS|PV:MIXED(6obj/1no_obj). Here the object (al-ākhirīna) IS explicit — the standard transitive reading. The Form II (faʿʿala) intensifies/makes causative the base root: Form I damara = to perish, to be destroyed (intransitive); Form II dammara = to cause to be destroyed utterly, to annihilate completely, to leave nothing standing. The attached pronoun nā = us (1st pl), making the subject explicit in the verb form: "we-destroyed." The rarity of this root (COUNT:10, uncommon) makes its selection here semantically deliberate — the Quran could have used ahlaka (far more common) but chose dammara for its intensity.

Verb, past tense (fiʿl māḍī), Form IV (afʿala: amṭara — "to cause rain to fall"), 1st person plural (naḥnu, "We" — divine plural of majesty), with pronominal subject suffix -nā. Form IV is causative of the base root: "to make rain fall, to shower down." The verb takes ʿalayhim (upon them) as the directional complement and maṭaran as a cognate accusative. No external source or agent named — God is the unnamed but implied source.
notes: cognate accusative present

grammar: Verb, past tense (fiʿl māḍī), Form I (saʾa — "to be evil/bad"), 3rd person masculine singular, with maṭaru al-mundhharīn as its subject. Sāʾa functions here as a verb of dhamm (condemnation/blame) in classical Arabic rhetoric — parallel to niʿma in structures of praise. The construction "sāʾa X" = "how evil was X!" or "X was vile." The sentence is a complete condemnation with no additional predicate needed.
perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), 3rd person masculine singular, copular function; aktharuhum = subject (ism kāna), muʾminīna = predicate (khabar kāna)

Verb (PV), Form II (faʿʿala), 3rd person masculine singular, active voice, past tense. From k-dh-b: "to lie, to be false." Form II kadhdhaba = to accuse someone of lying, to declare something false, to reject as untrue. ROOT_LEXICON: 282 occurrences, 122 PV, 61 IV; Form II active voice. Direct object: al-mursalīn (word 4). The verb carries not passive disbelief but active falsification — the accusers assert that the messengers are liars. Verb-initial position (VSO order) foregrounds the act of denial over the agents.

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject: Shuʿaybun. The verb introduces direct speech (maqūl al-qawl) extending to the end of the ayah. TRANSITIVITY: PV:MIXED(726obj/185no_obj) — overwhelmingly transitive; here the object is the quoted speech clause a-lā tattaqūna. q-w-l is the most frequent verbal root in the Quran (COUNT: 1337); its co-occurrence with sh-ʿ-b root (8 times, #1 co-occurrence for sh-ʿ-b) reflects the structural bond between the Shuʿayb narratives and speech-acts.

Imperfect verb (fiʿl muḍāriʿ), Form VIII (iftaʿala), 2nd person masculine plural, indicative. From root w-q-y: "to shield, protect, guard." Form VIII adds reflexive meaning: "to shield oneself, take precaution for oneself." The tāʾ of Form VIII assimilates with the wāw of the root, yielding the doubled tāʾ (tattaqī base form). w-q-y occurs 256 times in the Quran — IV:59, with TRANSITIVITY IV:MIXED(42obj/17no_obj). Here used without explicit object — the question is "will you not guard yourselves?" leaving open WHAT they should guard against. In the People of the Thicket context, the elided object anticipates the specific condemnation of their commercial dishonesty (26:181-183) and their mocking demand for punishment (26:187); taqwā means resisting both material greed and divine insolence.

Imperative (CV), Form VIII (iftaʿala), second person masculine plural. From w-q-y: "to protect, guard, shield." Form VIII reflexive: "protect oneself, guard oneself." Direct object: Allāha (accusative). ROOT_LEXICON: 256 Quranic occurrences, 92 CV, MIXED transitivity (90 obj / 2 no_obj). Addressed to the People of the Thicket/Aykah — a commercial community whom the Quran characterizes as practitioners of fraudulent measure-giving (shortchanging weight and scales: vv.181–183). The command to shield themselves through God is directed at a people whose implicit self-protection strategy is commercial advantage — Shuʿayb redirects: the real wiqāya is taqwā, not fraudulent profit.

Imperative (CV), Form IV (afʿala), second person masculine plural + nūn al-wiqāya + first-person singular pronoun (-nī contracted to -ni before pause). From ṭ-w-ʿ: "to obey, be willing, comply voluntarily." ROOT_LEXICON: 128 occurrences; 31 CV, 53 IV. The Form IV (causative/formal) is the standard Quranic obedience command. The nūn al-wiqāya protects the final vowel before the pronoun suffix. In the Shuʿayb/Aykah pericope, aṭīʿūni commands obedience specifically to Shuʿayb — a messenger whose authority was just established through the amīn declaration (26:178); obedience is now grounded in trust, not compulsion. The specific behavioral content of "obedience to me" will be disclosed immediately in 26:181–183 (full measure, honest balance, no defrauding).

Imperfect verb (IV or VIII-variant), 2nd person masculine plural. Root ṣ-l-y. PV (Form VIII perfect): 3rd person masculine singular perfect of ittabaʿa. Form VIII with reflexive/intensive nuance — "he deliberately followed." The shift from imperfect to perfect signals a transition from habitual behavior to settled condition.

The imperfect indicates ongoing or habitual action — they "keep saying" this, not as a one-time utterance but as a repeated pattern. Object is the entire quoted clause that follows (matā hādhā l-waʿdu in kuntum ṣādiqīna). MASAQ tags: IV (imperfect verb).

Perfect (māḍī) verb, Form I, 2nd person masculine plural. kāna + ṣādiqīna = compound predicate (kāna wa-akhawātuhā). The perfect tense here does not indicate past time but establishes a state: "if you are [= have been and continue to be] truthful." kāna with an active participle (ṣādiqīn) forms a continuous state construction. MASAQ tags: PV (perfect verb). Transitivity: MIXED (with_object: 773, without_object: 297) — here used without explicit object, as copular verb.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person masculine plural, active voice. From root n-ẓ-r. In this context: "they await / they expect." The verb n-ẓ-r carries dual semantics: visual perception ("to look, to see") and temporal expectation ("to wait for, to anticipate"). Here the mā...illā construction governs it: "they do not await anything except." The imperfect tense marks the awaiting as ongoing/habitual — they are in a continuous state of unknowing expectation.

Imperfect verb, Form I, 3rd person feminine singular, active voice + attached pronoun -hum (3rd person masculine plural, accusative — "them"). From root '-kh-dh. Subject is ṣayḥa (feminine) — the shout seizes them. The imperfect here functions as a narrative present or future-certain: the seizure has not yet happened but is presented as inevitable. The verb is TRANSITIVE with explicit object (-hum). The attached pronoun refers back to the subject of yanẓurūna — "them" = those who await.

Imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine plural, active voice. From root kh-ṣ-m. This form is morphologically unusual: the standard Form VIII would be yakhtaṣimūna (يَخْتَصِمُونَ), but in this reading (Hafs), the tāʾ of Form VIII has assimilated into the ṣād, producing yakhiṣṣimūna. Alternative canonical readings offer yakhaṣṣimūna, yakhṣṣimūna, yakhṣimūna — all reflecting different degrees of assimilation or simplification. The verb is INTRANSITIVE here (no explicit object) — MIXED transitivity in ROOT DATA (with_object: 3, without_object: 4), and 36:49 is among the without-object ayahs. The intransitive reading means "they dispute among themselves" — reciprocal, self-directed contention.

Form X (istafʿala) imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural. Form X of ṭ-w-ʿ: to seek compliance/obedience from something = to have it under one's power, to be able. The imperfect indicates ongoing state. With lā: absolute denial of capacity.

Form I imperfect indicative, 3rd person masculine plural. Active voice in the Hafs reading. The imperfect indicates attempted or expected action, here negated by the preceding lā. A qirāʾa reads yurjaʿūna (passive), shifting agency: "they are returned" vs "they return." Transitivity flag: MIXED — this verb can be transitive ("to return something") or intransitive ("to go back"). Here used intransitively (no direct object).

grammar: Perfect verb, Form I, 3rd person feminine singular, active voice. From root k-w-n. The tāʾ al-taʾnīth (feminine marker) agrees with the implied subject (the event/affair, al-wāqiʿa or al-qiṣṣa) or with the predicate ṣayḥa (feminine). In the qiraʾa variant (ṣayḥatun wāḥidatun, nominative), ṣayḥa becomes the explicit subject and kānat agrees with it directly. The perfect tense expresses certainty of a future event (taḥqīq) — the resurrection-shout is presented as already accomplished. MIXED transitivity in ROOT DATA (773 with object, 297 without). Here used without explicit object — the predicate is ṣayḥatan (accusative, predicate of kāna).

Intransitive here (no explicit object) — the mujrimūn are commanded to undergo separation, not to separate something else. MASAQ: CV role.

Perfect verb (fiʿl māḍī), 2nd person masculine plural. From root k-w-n (to be, to exist). Functions as the auxiliary component of a compound tense: kuntum + imperfect tūʿadūna = past continuous ("you were being promised"). Without an explicit object, kuntum here is used intransitively as a copular/existential verb. The MIXED transitivity flag in ROOT DATA (773 with object, 297 without) confirms this copular use is well-attested.

Form IV passive (yuʿadu → tūʿadūna), imperfect indicative, 2nd person masculine plural. The passive voice (mabnī li-l-majhūl) conceals the agent: who promised? God, prophets, warners, or the structure of reality itself? Combined with kuntum, this forms the past continuous: "you were continually being promised/warned." The imperfect inside the kāna-compound emphasizes repetition and habituality. Transitivity: MIXED (12 with object, 10 without in IV_PASS form). Here used without explicit object — what was promised is identified by the preceding jahannam, but the object elision in the verb itself creates semantic openness.

Form I imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive mood (majzūm after lā al-nāhiya). Root n-h-r: to rebuke with harshness, to repel by scolding. The object (al-sāʾila) is fronted via ammā. Only 2 verbal occurrences of n-h-r in the Quran: 17:23 (wa-lā tanharhumā — parents) and here. The root's 109 other occurrences are all nominal: nahār (daytime, 55x) and nahr (river, 54x).
verb, Form II imperative (faʿʿil pattern); 2nd person masculine singular; jussive/apocopated form
notes: حَدِّثْ takes a بِ complement here

grammar: imperfect verb, 1st person plural, jussive mood (apocopated by lam), Form I
perfect verb, 1st person plural, transitive, Form I
verb, Form IV (afʿala), perfect tense, 3rd person masculine singular, transitive; subject is wizraka (the burden) via alladhī
Perfect verb (PV), 1st person plural (majestic plural = divine "We"), transitive, Form I. The -nā suffix marks both the divine subject and the completed nature of the action. Direct object: dhikraka.

Perfect verb (PV), Form I, 2nd person masculine singular. Subject: the addressee (Prophet or any reader). The perfect tense within the idhā clause projects a future event as completed — grammatical certainty of finishing.

Imperative verb (CV), Form I, 2nd person masculine singular. The apocopated form (jazm) reflects the imperative mood. Root n-ṣ-b carries "to toil, to stand erect, to set up." The imperative commands strenuous effort immediately after completion. CV:1 in Quran — this is the sole imperative occurrence.
verb, imperative (CV), 2nd person masculine singular, Form I
perfect verb, 1st person plural (royal we / majestic plural), transitive with direct object al-insān
perfect verb, first person plural + third person masculine singular object pronoun; Form I (faʿala pattern); divine plural of majesty as agent

Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), Form IV (af'ala pattern: أَفْعَلَ → آمَنَ), third person masculine plural. The Form IV is causative/declarative: they caused themselves to enter a state of amn (security/trust). No explicit object — the verb is used intransitively here, though '-m-n IV is MIXED transitivity (137obj/43no_obj per ROOT LEXICON). The elided object opens interpretation: believed in God? in the message? in the process? The verb's absoluteness parallels 'amilū — both are unqualified, total commitments.

Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), Form I, third person masculine plural. Takes al-ṣāliḥāt as explicit direct object. MIXED transitivity (94obj/5no_obj for PV per ROOT LEXICON) — overwhelmingly transitive. The root '-m-l is fundamentally about productive action, labor, work that produces tangible results.
Form II imperfect indicative (muḍāriʿ marfūʿ), 3rd person masculine singular; subject is mā; object suffix -ka (2ms, addressed to the Prophet or to any human); IV tag in bundle = imperfect verb

Form I imperative verb, 2nd person masculine singular, with jazm (sukūn) on the hamza. From qara'a (to read, to recite, to gather). The hamza is retained in the standard Hafs reading. No explicit object -- the command is absolute, leaving what is to be read unspecified until 96:3 repeats the command.
notes: recitation object unexpressed

grammar: Form I perfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is the referent of alladhi (rabb). NO explicit object -- creation presented as absolute, objectless, universal. The verb stands alone to indicate the creative act without delimiting what was created.

Form I perfect verb (faʿala pattern), 3rd person masculine singular. Subject is Allāh (implied from context of 96:1). Takes al-insāna as direct object. MIXED transitivity: used both with and without explicit objects in the Quran.

Form I imperative (fi'l amr), 2nd person masculine singular, jussive (majzum). Root q-r-' yields qara'a/yaqra'u. This is the second occurrence of iqra' in the surah (first at 96:1), but here it stands alone without an object or prepositional phrase -- making the command absolute and unqualified.
notes: recitation object unexpressed

grammar: Form I (fa'ala) imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive mood (majzūm) due to preceding lam. Active voice. Intransitive here — no explicit object (the object is implied as mā, the antecedent of the relative clause). The jussive apocopation removes the final -u, producing ya'lam instead of ya'lamu.
Imperfect Form I verb, 3rd person masculine singular, active, indicative; intransitive (no explicit object); imperfect tense indicates habitual ongoing action — transgression as continuous state

Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular + attached object pronoun -hu. The pronoun can be reflexive (himself) or referential (him/another). Root r-'-y encompasses physical sight, mental perception, opinion-formation, and dream-vision. MIXED transitivity: 95 with object, 5 without in PV form.

Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), Form X (istaf'ala), 3rd person masculine singular. Form X of gh-n-y = to consider oneself ghaniyy (rich/self-sufficient), or to seek sufficiency. No explicit object — the verb can be transitive (he deemed X sufficient) or intransitive (he became/considered himself sufficient). MIXED transitivity: 9 with object, 7 without in PV form.

Perfect verb (fa'ala), Form I, 2nd person masculine singular, with interrogative hamza (أ) prefix. The hamza converts a declarative statement into a question. The verb is transitive here, taking the relative clause (alladhī yanhā) as its object. Combination of perfect tense + interrogative = rhetorical formula used for challenging the addressee to reflect.

Imperfect verb (muḍāri'), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, active voice. Used here WITHOUT an explicit direct object (intransitive use). The absence of an object leaves the scope of the prohibition open-ended. The imperfect tense marks the action as ongoing or habitual, not a single past event.
notes: local object continues in 96:10 outside ayah scope

grammar: Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), Form II (fa''ala pattern), third person masculine singular. Within the idhā clause, the perfect tense functions as a habitual present. Used here intransitively — no explicit object, paralleling 75:31 (fa-lā ṣaddaqa wa-lā ṣallā).

Perfect verb (Form I, fa'ala), 2nd person masculine singular, with interrogative hamza (أ) prefix. Transitive verb used here WITHOUT explicit object — one of only 5 objectless PV occurrences of this root (26:61, 41:52, 53:18, 96:11, 96:13). The object is the entire conditional clause that follows (إِن كَانَ عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ). Pragmatically, أَرَءَيْتَ has grammaticalized into a discourse marker meaning "consider this" or "tell me about."

Perfect verb (Form I), 3rd person masculine singular. In conditional context with إِنْ, كَانَ does not necessarily indicate past time — it marks a hypothetical state. Functions here as an incomplete verb (فعل ناقص) taking عَلَى ٱلْهُدَىٰ as its predicate (khabar). The subject is the person who forbids prayer (from 96:9-10). Mixed transitivity: 773 with object vs 297 without — here used without explicit object, with prepositional predicate instead.

Perfect verb (fi'l māḍī), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, active voice. Subject is implicit — referencing the person described in preceding context (the one who forbids, 96:9-10, now hypothetically reimagined as one who commands good). The verb governs bi-t-taqwā as its content complement via the preposition bā'.
notes: commanded content expressed by bi-phrase

grammar: Interrogative hamza (ʾa-) + perfect verb Form I (raʾā), 2nd person masculine singular with tāʾ al-fāʿil. Functions as a rhetorical formula rather than literal "seeing" — used to introduce a scenario for contemplation. No direct object in this ayah; the object is the entire conditional clause that follows.

Perfect verb (PV), Form II (faʿʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. Form II is intensive/causative of Form I (kadhaba = to lie): kadhdhaba = to accuse of lying, to declare something false, to actively reject as untrue. No explicit direct object — the denial is absolute and unqualified.
notes: object of denial not present locally

grammar: Perfect verb (PV), Form V (tafaʿʿala), 3rd person masculine singular. Form V of w-l-y: reflexive of Form II (wallā = to turn, to appoint). tawallā carries two opposing semantic vectors: (1) to turn away, to withdraw, to abandon; (2) to take charge of, to assume guardianship, to become walī of. No explicit object — the turning is absolute.

Imperfect verb (muḍāri'), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive mood (majzūm) governed by لَمْ. Active voice. Root '-l-m. Without explicit object here — the entire بِأَنَّ clause serves as the content of knowledge. Jussive apocopation visible in the sukūn on the final mīm.

Imperfect verb (muḍāri'), Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, indicative mood (marfū') — the alif maqṣūra (ىٰ) is the final radical. Active voice. No explicit object — making divine sight absolute and unbounded. Functions as the predicate (khabar) of the أَنَّ clause.

Form VIII (iftaʿala) imperfect verb, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive mood (apocopated — final yā' dropped by lam). Form VIII of n-h-y adds reflexive meaning: 'to forbid oneself, to restrain oneself, to desist.' Intransitive here (no explicit object). The verb is in the without_object category (7 intransitive uses in Quran).

Form I imperfect verb, 1st person plural (divine 'We'), with energetic nūn suffix (-an written as alif with tanwīn). The only occurrence of this root in the entire Quran. Transitivity: INTRANSITIVE per bundle (0 with object, 1 without) — the bā' preposition in bi-n-nāṣiyati supplies the complement.
notes: seizing expressed with bi-phrase

grammar: Imperfect verb Form I, 3rd person masculine singular, jussive mood (majzūm — final wāw deleted by jazm); governed by lām al-amr; subject is the unnamed transgressor from 96:9-10

Future particle سَ (sa-, indicating near/certain future) prefixed to Form IV imperfect first-person plural verb نَدْعُ (nad'u). The apocopated form (without final alif) is standard in Quranic rasm. Active voice, indicative mood (marfu'), first-person plural (royal "we" = divine self-reference).

Form IV imperfect verb, 2nd person masculine singular, jussive mood (majzūm by preceding lā nāhiya). Active voice. Attached pronoun -hu (him) as direct object. The jussive is marked by sukūn on the 'ayn (tuṭi' rather than tuṭī'u).

Imperative verb (fi'l amr), 2nd person masculine singular. From base Form I sajada. The imperative is formed from the imperfect yasjudu with deletion of the prefix and addition of hamzat al-waṣl. Jussive/imperative mood.

Form VIII imperative verb (fi'l amr), 2nd person masculine singular. ifta'ala pattern (iqtaraba). The tā' infix of Form VIII adds a reflexive/effort nuance — 'bring yourself near' rather than simple 'be near'. Jussive/imperative mood.
